finding.title: Missing ValidatorSet conflict token on governance/token_factory txs → parallel-batch clobber of staking::ValidatorSet → unbounded AIN mint via repeatable withdraw_unbonded
finding.mechanism: `analyze_tx` assigns conflict tokens per module. The `token_factory` branch (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2288-2317) declares deps {sender, resource_0x1_0x1::token_factory::TokenRegistry, resource_{sender}_TokenWallet} and the `governance` branch (:2276-2287) declares {sender, resource_0x1_0x1::governance::GovernanceState, resource_{sender}_VoteEscrow}. Neither declares `resource_{0x1}_0x1::staking::ValidatorSet` or `..._0x1::staking::SupplyStats` — but BOTH modules mutate them: token_factory::create_token calls `staking::burn_ain(fee)` (core/vm_move/stdlib/sources/token_factory.move:86-87) and governance::create_proposal calls `staking::burn_ain(fee_coins)` (governance.move:51-52), and `burn_ain` does `borrow_global_mut<ValidatorSet>(@0x1)` + `borrow_global_mut<SupplyStats>` (staking.move:528-547), so the Move ChangeSet emits Modify ops for both resource keys (core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:614-630 emits only modified resources, key = `resource_{addr}_{struct_tag}`). Meanwhile the `staking` branch (:2240-2245) declares deps {sender, validator_set_key(), sys:validator_set:v1}. The two dep sets are DISJOINT when the senders differ, so `schedule_batches` (:2352-2390) places them in the SAME parallel batch. Each tx is executed by `execute_transaction` against the PRE-batch DB only (documented at :2394-2405 — 'performs only reads against self.db'), so both compute a full ValidatorSet blob from the same base. The commit loop then sorts results by tx_hash (:1592) and pushes every tx's updates into one RocksDB WriteBatch (:1599-1608) — last put to a key wins. The ValidatorSet blob of whichever tx hashes higher therefore silently ERASES the other tx's ValidatorSet mutation, while that tx's writes to OTHER keys (its CoinStore) survive. `staking::withdraw_unbonded` (staking.move:304-333) is exactly that split: it removes the unbonding entry from ValidatorSet (clobberable key) and separately does `coin::mint` + `coin::deposit` into `resource_{addr}_CoinStore` (non-clobbered key). It also never touches `total_supply`, so nothing in the supply trackers records the mint.
finding.exploit_sequence:
Precondition: attacker controls two accounts — V, which previously called leave_validator_set and holds an unbonding request of, say, 1,000,000 AIN whose unlock_time has passed; and A, holding 100 AIN + gas.
1. Attacker submits tx_V = EntryFunction `0x1::staking::withdraw_unbonded()` from V. analyze_tx → deps {V, resource_00..01_0x1::staking::ValidatorSet, sys:validator_set:v1}. Its writes: ValidatorSet (queue entry removed) and resource_V_CoinStore<AincoreCoin> (+1,000,000 AIN freshly minted by coin::mint at staking.move:331).
2. Attacker submits tx_A = `0x1::token_factory::create_token(...)` from A, grinding a free field (gas_limit, token name/icon_url bytes) until sha256(tx_A_json) > sha256(tx_V_json). analyze_tx → deps {A, TokenRegistry@0x1, TokenWallet@A}. Its writes: ValidatorSet (total_supply -= 100 AIN, unbonding_queue = the PRE-batch queue, i.e. V's entry still present), SupplyStats, resource_A_CoinStore, TokenRegistry, TokenWallet@A.
3. Both txs land in one block. No shared conflict token → schedule_batches puts them in the same batch → rayon executes them in parallel, both reading the pre-batch ValidatorSet.
4. results.sort_by(tx_hash) (:1592) orders tx_A last; write_batch.put(resource_00..01_0x1::staking::ValidatorSet, tx_A's blob) (:1604) overwrites tx_V's blob.
5. Post-commit state: V's CoinStore is +1,000,000 AIN, AND V's unbonding request is still in ValidatorSet.unbonding_queue.
6. Repeat step 1+2 every block. Each round mints another 1,000,000 AIN for a cost of 100 AIN + gas.
The MAX_SUPPLY tripwire at core/executor/src/lib.rs:995 never fires because withdraw_unbonded never increments ValidatorSet.total_supply, and `distribute_rewards`' anchor `minted = total_supply + cumulative_burned` (staking.move:390) is likewise blind to it. The sort is deterministic, so every node commits the same clobber — no fork, the whole network accepts the phantom AIN.
Mirror-image variants of the same bug (attacker tx sorts EARLIER): tx_V = join_validator_set / add_stake — the victim's CoinStore is debited but the ValidatorSet update is erased, so the stake is destroyed while sys:validator_set:v1 (staged separately at :2828-2860) still lists them, desyncing the QC trust root from the Move validator set. Or the burn's ValidatorSet decrement is erased while its SupplyStats increment survives → `minted` inflates by the burn amount and `remaining` shrinks permanently (silent under-emission + permanently wrong circulating supply).
finding.impact: Unbounded inflation of AIN with no upper limit and no tripwire — the 150M hard cap is defeated outright for ~100 AIN per round. Directly fatal for the DEX float: minted AIN can be sold into the AMM. Secondary variants destroy user stake and desync the QC trust root from the Move validator set.
finding.suggested_fix: In `analyze_tx`, add `validator_set_key()` and `supply_stats_key()` to the dep set of EVERY module whose entry functions can reach `staking::burn_ain` — at minimum the `governance` branch (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2276) and both `token_factory` branches (:2288, :2307). Better: make the safety boundary structural rather than an allowlist — derive conflict tokens from a per-entry-function declared write set, or run any tx that can transitively touch a 0x1 global singleton in its own singleton batch. As defence in depth, add an assertion in the commit loop that no two txs in one batch emit an update for the same key (panic/serialize instead of silently last-write-wins), which would have caught this class at the first occurrence.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every link in the chain is present in the source.

1. `analyze_tx` conflict tokens — core/executor/src/lib.rs:2174. Unconditional deps are only `sender_token` (:2188), the paymaster token (:2201-2208), and `tx.input_objects` (:2210-2212). No unconditional ValidatorSet/SupplyStats token.
   - staking branch, lib.rs:2239-2245: `recognized = true; deps.push(validator_set_key()); deps.push(validator_set_v1_key())`.
   - governance branch, lib.rs:2274-2286: `recognized = true;` deps = GovernanceState@0x1 + VoteEscrow@sender only. **No validator_set_key, no supply_stats_key.**
   - token_factory catch-all, lib.rs:2303-2317: deps = TokenRegistry@0x1 + TokenWallet@sender only. Same omission.
   `validator_set_key()` is defined at lib.rs:290-296 as `resource_{0x1}_0x1::staking::ValidatorSet`.

2. Both omitted branches really do mutate ValidatorSet. `governance::create_proposal` (core/vm_move/stdlib/sources/governance.move:40-52) calls `staking::burn_ain(fee_coins)`; `burn_ain` (staking.move:528-547) does `borrow_global_mut<ValidatorSet>(@0x1)` + `borrow_global_mut<SupplyStats>(@0x1)`. `token_factory::create_token` (token_factory.move:86-87) does the same.

3. The Move ChangeSet emits a Modify op for those resources, keyed exactly `resource_{addr}_{struct_tag}` — core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:613-632 (`changeset_to_kv`). Those go straight into the tx's update vec via `absorb_vm_result!` at core/executor/src/lib.rs:2732-2740.

4. Parallel sessions are genuinely independent reads of pre-batch state: `execute_transaction_actions` does `self.vm.new_session(&self.storage)` (core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:472) and `AINCOREStorage` is a read-through resolver over `StateDB` — nothing writes back into it between txs. The doc comment at lib.rs:2394-2405 states the same contract.

5. `schedule_batches` (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2408-2440) only splits on token overlap. Two `recognized=true` txs with disjoint deps and different senders land in the SAME batch.

6. The commit loop is unguarded last-write-wins: `results.sort_by(tx_hash)` at lib.rs:1592, then a single `WriteBatch` with `write_batch.put(key, val)` per update at :1599-1608. There is no same-key assertion. The batch hasher folds both writes, so every node commits the identical clobber — deterministic, no fork, no alarm.

7. `withdraw_unbonded` (staking.move:304-333) is exactly the split the claim describes: it mutates ValidatorSet (`vector::remove` from `unbonding_queue`) and separately does `coin::mint<AincoreCoin>(amount)` + `coin::deposit(addr, coins)` into `resource_{addr}_CoinStore` — and never touches `total_supply`. So `append_supply_tracker_updates` (lib.rs:975-1011) sees no supply delta and the MAX_SUPPLY tripwire at :995 never fires.

CORRECTIONS to the claim (it over-reached on economics, not on mechanism):
- The 100-AIN `token_factory::create_token` route is NOT live. `TokenRegistry` is never created at genesis — core/node/src/genesis.rs initializes ValidatorSet, Epoch, GovernanceState, Treasury, DeviceRegistry, OracleConfig, dex::PoolRegistry (lines 969-1139) but no TokenRegistry — and `token_factory::initialize` (token_factory.move:56) is `public fun`, not `public entry fun`, with no Rust caller (grep over core/node, core/executor, core/vm_move finds none). `create_token` therefore aborts at `borrow_global_mut<TokenRegistry>(@0x1)` (token_factory.move:98).
- The live carrier is `governance::create_proposal`, whose GovernanceState IS genesis-initialized (genesis.rs:1026-1031) and which is a plain `public entry fun` with no gate. Its burn is 10,000 AIN (governance.move:49), not 100 — so the per-round cost is 100x the claim.
- The unbounded-mint variant additionally needs the attacker to have been a validator, called `leave_validator_set` (staking.move:212-252, MIN_STAKE = 1e21 = 1,000 AIN, staking.move:28), and waited `UNBONDING_PERIOD = 1,814,400` against `current_time = current_epoch * EPOCH_SECONDS(60)` (staking.move:82-86, 239-240) = 30,240 epochs ≈ 604,800 blocks. Not reachable on the current ~350k-round testnet; reachable within mainnet lifetime. Profitable only if the unbonded stake exceeds the 10,000 AIN proposal fee — trivially arranged by staking e.g. 50,000 AIN.
- Tx-hash grinding is real: `tx_hash_hex(raw)` hashes the raw JSON and the attacker owns the signing key, so gas_limit/description bytes can be re-ground and re-signed freely to force the desired sort order.

What IS reachable today, with no unbonding wait: any `governance::create_proposal` sharing a block with any staking tx silently corrupts the ValidatorSet singleton. If the governance tx sorts later, a victim's `add_stake`/`join_validator_set` has its CoinStore debit survive while its ValidatorSet update is erased — stake destroyed — and because `append_validator_set_v1_update` / `refresh_validator_set_v1_stake` stage `sys:validator_set:v1` separately (lib.rs:2828-2860), the QC trust root desyncs from the Move validator set. If it sorts earlier, the burn's `total_supply` decrement is erased while the SupplyStats increment survives, permanently inflating the `minted = total_supply + cumulative_burned` emission anchor (staking.move:390).

This is not covered by the prior paymaster conflict-token fix (lib.rs:2195-2208), which tokenized only the paymaster address. The comment at lib.rs:2167-2173 claims the allowlist is "a fast PATH for known calls, NEVER the safety boundary" — but for `recognized=true` branches it IS the safety boundary, and here it is under-declared.

Suggested fix direction is sound: add `validator_set_key()` + `supply_stats_key()` to the governance, token_factory, and delegation branches (delegation.move:149/228/317/394 reaches `staking::mint_delegation_reward`, which mutates `EmissionPools@0x1` — also undeclared, currently harmless only because DELEGATION_BPS=0), and add a same-key assertion in the batch commit loop at lib.rs:1596-1610 as a structural backstop.

finding.title: Anchor selection falls back to a backup leader based purely on LOCAL DAG availability — two honest nodes finalize different anchors (and different blocks) for the same round
finding.mechanism: `try_commit` picks the anchor by looping `for attempt in 0..max_attempts` (ordering.rs:504-537). On each attempt it asks `get_leader_with_fallback` for a leader and then searches `round_index[anchor_round]` for a vertex authored by that leader. If the primary leader's vertex is not present IN THIS NODE'S LOCAL DAG at that instant, it silently falls through to the next leader and commits that one instead. There is no timeout, no certificate of the primary leader's absence, and no cross-node agreement on the fallback. The support check that follows (ordering.rs:556-579) does not disambiguate at all: `try_create_vertex` sets `parents = round_idx[prev_round]` (dag.rs:333-339), i.e. every round-R+1 vertex lists EVERY round-R vertex it holds as a parent, so in a healthy DAG *every* round-R vertex has ~100% of round-R+1 vertices voting for it and therefore passes the >2/3 stake-quorum test. The leader-election loop is the ONLY thing selecting the anchor, and it is a function of local message arrival, not of committed state.
finding.exploit_sequence: n=3 validators V1/V2/V3, equal stake. At round R the elected leader is V1. V1's round-R vertex reaches V2 and V3 but the gossip copy to V3 is dropped/delayed (ordinary UDP/gossipsub loss, or a Byzantine V1 that simply withholds it from V3 — no equivocation needed). Round R+1 and R+2 proceed normally. V3 processes a round-R+2 vertex → `try_commit(R+2)` → anchor_round=R → attempt 0 elects V1 → `round_index[R]` has no V1 vertex on V3 → attempt 1 elects, say, V2 → V2's round-R vertex IS present and is supported by all three round-R+1 vertices → V3 commits anchor = V2's vertex. V1 and V2 commit anchor = V1's vertex. Result at the same anchor round R: V1/V2 build block #H with `commit.sequence` = causal history of V1's vertex and `reward_recipient = V1`; V3 builds block #H with a different sequence and `reward_recipient = V2`. Different tx set, different fee/reward recipient, different `state_root`, different block hash — both are 'final' (`committed_rounds.insert(R)`, `finalized_round = R`, dag.rs:911-945 persists the block).
finding.impact: Permanent chain fork with ZERO Byzantine participants required. Two conflicting blocks at the same height both reach local finality on honest nodes. Because sync/src/lib.rs:904-917 explicitly refuses a state-changing reorg, the nodes never reconcile. No QC can ever form for the forked heights (QC votes bind block_hash, qc_producer.rs:353-357), so bridge/light-client finality silently stops. On mainnet with a live DEX this means two disjoint views of user balances.
finding.suggested_fix: Make anchor selection a pure function of committed state, not of local availability. Either (a) remove the fallback entirely — if the elected leader's vertex is absent, return None and retry on the next vertex (Bullshark's actual rule: an anchor is skipped only when >2/3 of round R+1 vertices demonstrably do NOT reference it, which is a quorum-certified fact every node computes identically), or (b) make the fallback quorum-certified: only advance to attempt k+1 when >2/3 stake of round-R+1 vertices are present AND none of them lists a leader-k vertex as a parent. Add a cross-node determinism test: two engines with DIFFERENT DAG subsets (one missing the leader's vertex) must either commit the same anchor or both commit nothing.

verdict.reasoning:
The mechanism is real in the deployed code; the auditor's specific n=3 exploit sequence is WRONG, but a corrected sequence works.

WHAT THE SOURCE CONFIRMS:
1. consensus/consensus/src/ordering.rs:504-537 — `for attempt in 0..max_attempts { let leader_id = self.get_leader_with_fallback(anchor_round, validators, attempt); if let Some(hashes) = round_index.get(&anchor_round) { ...find(|h| dag.get(h).author == leader_id)... } }`. The ONLY predicate for skipping the elected leader is "no vertex authored by it exists in THIS node's local `round_index[anchor_round]` right now". No timeout, no quorum-certified absence proof, no cross-node agreement. `get_leader_with_fallback` itself (ordering.rs:680-750) IS deterministic (seed = round + step1_beacon + attempt, stake-weighted walk over canonically-sorted validators) — the non-determinism comes purely from which `attempt` index each node stops at, which is local-view dependent.
2. The support check at ordering.rs:556-579 does not disambiguate. `try_create_vertex` sets `parents = round_idx[prev_round].clone()` (dag.rs:333-339), i.e. every R+1 vertex lists every locally-held round-R vertex, so a backup anchor is supported by essentially every R+1 vertex a node holds.
3. No causal-completeness gate: `add_vertex` (dag.rs:634-822) validates round bounds, timestamp drift, Ed25519 sig, hash recompute, validator-set membership and equivocation — it NEVER requires the vertex's parents to be present locally, and there is no missing-parent fetch anywhere (grep for request/fetch vertex finds nothing). So a node with a hole at round R keeps ingesting R+1/R+2 and reaches commit.
4. `try_commit` has exactly one live call site — dag.rs:859, invoked from `add_vertex` on every ingested vertex with the node's own `dag`/`round_index` — so the local-view input is the deployed path. The commit is immediately turned into a block and persisted (dag.rs:910-945, `save_block_json`), and QC production is explicitly "ADDITIVE & SIDE-EFFECT-ONLY … NOT a precondition for commit" (dag.rs:989-997), so nothing gates local finality on network agreement.
5. No reconciliation: sync/src/lib.rs:904-923 refuses a state-changing reorg (keeps the local fork), and sync/src/lib.rs:869-880 rejects any conflict at/below `finalized_round`.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS WRONG: the stated n=3 equal-stake sequence does NOT work. `qc::stake_quorum_met(s,t) = s*3 > t*2` (strict). With 3 equal-stake validators, the deprived node V3 holding only 2 of 3 round-R vertices fails the parent quorum in try_create_vertex (dag.rs:360-379, 2/3 is not >2/3), so V3 produces NO round-R+1 vertex; its vote round then holds only V1+V2 = 2/3 stake, which fails ordering.rs:573 and returns None. n=3 equal stake therefore halts (liveness), it does not fork. The auditor's "supported by all three round-R+1 vertices" is factually false in their own scenario.

CORRECTED, REACHABLE SEQUENCE: the divergence requires the deprived node to still hold >2/3 stake without the leader, i.e. n>=4 (equal stake: 3 of 4 = 75% > 66.7%, verified) or n=3 with unequal stake (e.g. 40/30/30, deprived of the 30-stake leader: 70/100 passes). At n=4: Byzantine-but-non-equivocating leader L broadcasts its round-R vertex to V2/V3 but withholds it from X (or plain gossip loss/late delivery, or X restarting and rejoining mid-round — dag.rs:200-260 only rehydrates vertices it actually received, so rounds missed while offline are permanent holes). X still forms its R+1 vertex from the other 3 parents. V2/V3/L commit anchor = L's vertex (3 of 4 R+1 vertices name it, 75% > 2/3). X's attempt 0 finds no L vertex, falls to attempt 1, elects backup B, whose R vertex is supported by all 4 R+1 vertices → X commits anchor = B. Both sides set `committed_rounds.insert(R)` / `finalized_round = R` (ordering.rs:593-595) and build a block at the same height with a different `commit.sequence`, different `reward_recipient` (dag.rs:870) and different state_root/hash. The rolling `finality_digest` (ordering.rs:623) and thus `step1_beacon` also diverge, so every subsequent leader election diverges — the fork is permanent, and sync refuses to heal it once the orphan blocks contain transactions (sync/src/lib.rs:892-923; note empty heartbeat blocks WOULD roll back and self-heal, which is why a quiet testnet can mask this).

NOT ALREADY FIXED: the H-1 fix in this area (ordering.rs:692-706) only made the election BEACON deterministic (`step1_beacon` instead of QC-folded `last_vdf_output`); it explicitly did not touch the availability-driven `attempt` fallback, which is the remaining divergence source.

finding.title: Committed partition (and therefore finality_digest and the leader-election beacon) depends on local vertex arrival order — one skipped anchor round permanently forks leader election on that node
finding.mechanism: `try_commit` is driven exclusively by `add_vertex` with the INCOMING vertex's round (`engine.try_commit(vertex.round, ...)`, dag.rs:859) and only ever attempts the single anchor `current_round - 2` (ordering.rs:479). The anti-double-commit guard `anchor_round <= self.finalized_round` (ordering.rs:487-491) is monotonic, so if a node ever processes a round r' vertex before a round r<r' vertex, anchor r'-2 is committed first and anchor r-2 is skipped FOREVER — there is no catch-up loop. Skipping is not benign because two commit-critical values are derived from the commit PARTITION rather than from the committed SET: (1) `finality_digest = H(prev_digest || h1 || h2 …)` folded per-commit (ordering.rs:623), and (2) the leader-election beacon `step1_beacon = VDF(anchor_round || finality_digest)` (ordering.rs:664, 293-305), which `get_leader_with_fallback` reads to elect every subsequent anchor leader (ordering.rs:707). Two nodes that committed the same vertices but partitioned into a different number of commits produce different digests, hence different beacons, hence different leaders for every later round.
finding.exploit_sequence: Node A and node B both hold the identical DAG. Node A receives a round-12 vertex before any round-11 vertex (ordinary gossip reorder, or a Byzantine peer that sends A its round-12 vertex first). A: `try_commit(12)` → commits anchor 10 (its causal history transitively includes round-9 vertices); then `try_commit(11)` → anchor 9 ≤ finalized_round(10) → skipped forever. B receives in order: commits anchor 9 (sequence S9), then anchor 10 (sequence S10\S9). A's digest = H(prev || sort(S9 ∪ S10)); B's = H(H(prev || sort(S9)) || sort(S10\S9)). Different strings → different `step1_beacon` → `get_leader_with_fallback(anchor_round=11, …)` derives `vdf_seed` from different bytes → A and B elect DIFFERENT leaders for anchor round 11 → they commit different anchors → fully divergent chains from that point on. A is also permanently one block behind B (`latest_block_height += 1` per commit, dag.rs:910), so height H means different blocks on the two nodes.
finding.impact: Permanent fork + double finality reachable from benign network reordering, no Byzantine node needed. Also makes the block height↔round mapping node-local, so `handle_remote_qc_vote`'s `block_{height}` binding (dag.rs:1544-1555) compares the wrong blocks and QC assembly stops.
finding.suggested_fix: Decouple commit from arrival order: on every `try_commit`, iterate anchors from `finalized_round + 1` up to `current_round - 2` in ascending order and commit each one that meets quorum, so the commit partition is a deterministic function of the DAG contents rather than of message order. Separately, derive the leader-election beacon for round R from state that is fixed for round R (e.g. the digest at `finalized_round` of a fixed lag below R, or the QC at R - k) rather than from 'whatever this node committed most recently'. Add a test that feeds two engines the same vertices in different orders and asserts identical `finality_digest`, identical block boundaries, and identical leaders.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried hard to refute this and could not. The three code facts the claim rests on are all exactly as stated, and I found no guard, no catch-up loop, and no repair path.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED IN SOURCE

1. Single-anchor, arrival-driven commit with a monotonic permanent skip.
   - `consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:859` — `engine.try_commit(vertex.round, &dag, &round_idx, &validators)`, driven by the INCOMING vertex's round. `grep -rn try_commit` returns exactly one call site (dag.rs:859) plus the definition — there is no loop, no tick-driven catch-up, no `for r in finalized_round+1..=current-2`.
   - `consensus/consensus/src/ordering.rs:479` — `let anchor_round = current_round - 2;` only ever one anchor attempted.
   - `consensus/consensus/src/ordering.rs:487-491` — `if self.committed_rounds.contains(&anchor_round) || (self.finalized_round > 0 && anchor_round <= self.finalized_round) { return None; }`, and `ordering.rs:595` `self.finalized_round = self.finalized_round.max(anchor_round);` is monotonic. So once anchor R+1 commits, anchor R can never commit. Permanent, confirmed.
   - Re-delivery does NOT give a retry: `dag.rs:732-735` drops duplicate hashes and `return`s from `add_vertex` BEFORE the ordering block, so a re-gossiped vertex never re-fires `try_commit`.

2. The digest is a function of the commit PARTITION, not the committed SET.
   - `ordering.rs:430-437` `fold_finality_digest(prev, new) = H(prev || h1 || h2 …)`. H(H(x‖S9)‖S10) ≠ H(x‖S9∪S10). Confirmed partition-dependent.
   - `ordering.rs:623-624` folds per commit; `ordering.rs:664` → `update_random_beacon(anchor_round, &digest)` → `ordering.rs:293-305` sets `step1_beacon = VDF(beacon_challenge(anchor_round, finality_digest))`.
   - `ordering.rs:707` `let election_beacon = &self.step1_beacon;` → `ordering.rs:730-747` stake-weighted draw seeded from it. So a divergent digest elects divergent anchor leaders for every later round. Confirmed.

3. No structural ordering protection at ingestion.
   - `dag.rs:634-821` `add_vertex` validates round ceiling, timestamp drift, pubkey, signature, hash recomputation, validator membership — but there is NO parent-availability check and no missing-parent buffer. A round-R+2 vertex is accepted with none of its round-R+1 parents present.
   - `dag.rs:1580-1584` `handle_message` → `add_vertex` directly; `core/node/src/main.rs:676-685` (gossipsub) and `:724-731` (TCP server) both call it with no reordering queue.

WHY THE CLAIM'S OWN EXPLOIT SEQUENCE IS WRONG (but the bug survives a corrected one)
The stated sequence — "A receives a round-12 vertex before any round-11 vertex, `try_commit(12)` commits anchor 10" — cannot happen. `ordering.rs:548-549` does `let votes = round_index.get(&vote_round)?` on round 11, and `ordering.rs:556-579` requires >2/3 STAKE of distinct round-11 authors. With no round-11 vertices there is no commit. Reordering one vertex is not sufficient.

The reachable version needs a genuine GAP in the local DAG at the instant a later-round vertex arrives. Two variants, both live-reachable:
(a) Missing quorum member at the vote round. Live stakes (docs/MULTI_VALIDATOR_BRINGUP.md:53-55: 1M / 2M / 1.5M, total 4.5M; `qc.rs:194-196` requires signed*3 > total*2, i.e. >3M) make the quorum sets exactly {val2,val3} and {val1,val2,val3} — val1 is NOT quorum-necessary. So val1 can commit anchor R+1 purely off val2+val3 vertices without ever having produced its own round-R+2 vertex. - Dual transports (gossipsub at main.rs:676 and TCP at main.rs:724) deliver concurrently into the same `RwLock`, acquired in arbitrary order.

That is a consensus-safety break reachable with zero Byzantine participants, causing unrecoverable validator loss — HIGH, not CRITICAL.

The suggested fix is directionally right: iterate anchors ascending from `finalized_round + 1` to `current_round - 2` on every `try_commit` so the commit partition is a function of DAG contents rather than message arrival, and add the two-engines-different-order determinism test.

round2_verdicts.title: abort-partial-commit
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
Confirmed by source reading AND an executed end-to-end PoC (test added, run, then reverted — working tree clean).

MECHANISM (three links, all verified in source):

1. move-vm has no undo log. `Session::execute_entry_function` (~/.cargo/git/checkouts/move-5734c3a45f62af74/281f7ec/language/move-vm/runtime/src/session.rs:72-91) mutates `self.data_cache` in place. `TransactionDataCache::into_effects` (data_cache.rs:75-140) emits an `Op::Modify` for every `GlobalValue` whose status is `Dirty`, and `GlobalValueImpl::into_effect` (move-vm/types/src/values/values_impl.rs:2524-2536) has no notion of "the call that dirtied me aborted". `mark_dirty` (values_impl.rs:279) fires on the `borrow_global_mut` write itself. The adapter contract is therefore: DISCARD the session on abort. Aptos does this; AINCORE does not.

2. core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:462-557 `execute_transaction_actions`. On a non-`must_succeed` action failure it does NOT drop the session: lines 541-550 only print "⚠️ Payload execution failed (state reverted)" (the message is factually false) and set `status = ExecutionStatus::aborted(...)`, then falls through to line 553-554 `session.finish()` → `changeset_to_kv(changeset)` and returns `Ok((gas, vm_changes, aborted_status))` with the partial writes inside `vm_changes`.

3. core/executor/src/lib.rs:2739-2757 `absorb_vm_result!`. The `for (k, v) in $vm_changes { updates.push((k, v)); }` loop runs BEFORE the `if !$status.success` check — the changes are staged unconditionally; the status only sets the receipt string to "aborted". The function then returns `Some((updates, actual_gas))` (lines 2959-2966), and `execute_block_parallel` (lines 1598-1614) writes every returned key into the RocksDB `WriteBatch` and folds it into `sys:state_root`. There is no filter on tx_status anywhere on that path.

PoC (executed, passed): `coin::transfer<AincoreCoin>` of 100 from a funded sender to a recipient with no CoinStore. `coin::withdraw` debits at coin.move:74, then `coin::deposit` aborts at coin.move:53. Result printed: `sender_balance_after_aborted_transfer=899900` (1,000,000 − 100,000 gas − 100). Reverted semantics would give 900,000. The 100 AIN was destroyed by a transaction the receipt marks "aborted".

REACHABILITY — reachable from any ordinary user transaction, no privilege needed, and worse than "one bad stdlib function":

(a) Ordinary-user fund destruction: `coin::transfer` to any address without a registered CoinStore silently burns the amount (proven above). Same shape in `staking::withdraw_unbonded` (staking.move:304-332): `vector::remove` deletes the unbonding entry from `ValidatorSet`, then `coin::deposit` aborts if no CoinStore → the entire unbonded stake is erased with nothing paid out.

(b) Instruction-granularity halt primitive. core/vm_move/src/gas.rs:48-60 returns `EXECUTION_LIMIT_REACHED` from `charge()`, which propagates as a normal `Err` into the exact same non-fatal branch at lib.rs:541. `gas_limit` is fully attacker-chosen. So an attacker can stop ANY entry function at ANY instruction boundary and keep everything written up to that point. That turns every credit-before-debit sequence into a mint. Example: `delegation::claim_rewards` (delegation.move:299-333) does `coin::deposit(delegator_addr, reward_coins)` and only AFTERWARDS updates `d.reward_debt`; halting between them keeps the reward and leaves `reward_debt` stale → repeatable reward minting. Same shape in `delegation::undelegate` (delegation.move:222-231 deposit, 236-253 the bookkeeping that follows).

(c) DEX brick, zero capital, directly on the founder's launch path: `dex::add_liquidity` (dex.move:93-151) executes `pool.lp_supply = pool.lp_supply + MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY;` at line 115 BEFORE `assert!(liquidity >= min_lp, ...)` at line 136. Any user calls `add_liquidity<X,Y>(pool_addr, amount_x, amount_y, min_lp = u128::MAX)` against a freshly created empty pool: the assert aborts, `coin::withdraw` (line 139) never runs so no tokens are spent, but `lp_supply` is committed as 1000 with zero reserves. The pool is then permanently dead — `lp_supply != 0` routes all future calls to the else-branch, which aborts at line 119 `assert!(reserve_x > 0 && reserve_y > 0)`, and `create_pool` (dex.move:63-90) refuses to re-register the canonical pair (line 71 `!pool_exists(&registry.pools, &pool_key)`). Cost: one tx of gas.

No guard prevents any of this: no friend/visibility restriction is relevant (the entry points are `public entry`), mempool does not gate `gas_limit` downward, and there is no post-execution revert filter. Severity CRITICAL is honest and if anything understated — this is a failure of transaction atomicity itself, so every `assert!` placed after a mutation anywhere in the stdlib (present or future) is a live bug, and the executor's own log line asserts the opposite of what happens.

NOTE for the fix author: the single shared session is deliberate — the `deduct_gas` pre-action (executor lib.rs:2684-2693, `must_succeed = true`) must survive the user's abort. A naive "drop the session on abort" would also drop the gas charge and make aborts free (a spam vector). See minimal_fix.
round2_verdicts.minimal_fix:
Split the single session in `execute_transaction_actions` (core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:462-557) into two, Aptos-style, so the user payload's changeset is discarded wholesale on abort while gas still lands:

1. Session U (user payload only): run the non-`must_succeed` actions. If any returns `Err`, DROP the session without calling `finish()` — do not compute or return its changeset. `user_changes = vec![]`, status = aborted. Only on full success do `finish()` → `changeset_to_kv`.
2. Session G (gas/system pre-actions): run the `must_succeed` actions in a SEPARATE session whose resolver is `AINCOREStorage` overlaid with `user_changes` (an in-memory delta layered over the RocksDB reads in `ModuleResolver`/`ResourceResolver`), so the gas debit applies on top of a successful payload and on top of untouched state after an abort. Always commit `gas_changes`.
3. Return `(gas_used, gas_changes ++ user_changes, status)`. Keep the single shared `AINCOREGasMeter` across both sessions so metering is unchanged.
4. Fix the lying log at lib.rs:545 and add a regression test asserting that a `coin::transfer` to an unregistered recipient leaves the sender at `pre_balance - gas` (900_000 in the harness above), not `pre_balance - gas - amount`.

Independently of the VM fix, move the pre-assert mutation in dex.move:115 (`pool.lp_supply = pool.lp_supply + MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY`) below the `min_lp` / `liquidity` asserts at lines 135-137 — defense in depth for the launch-critical pool.

round2_verdicts.title: dex-brick
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
Confirmed by source reading AND an executed end-to-end PoC through the real executor path (test added temporarily, run, then reverted; working tree restored).

1) The abort-partial-commit premise is REAL, not theoretical.
- core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:541-556 (`execute_transaction_actions`): when an action fails with `must_succeed == false` (which is exactly how a user EntryFunction is pushed — core/executor/src/lib.rs:2817-2821 passes `false`), the code only records `status = ExecutionStatus::aborted(...)`, then unconditionally calls `session.finish()` (line 553) and returns the changeset.
- move-vm has no intra-session rollback. `Session::finish` → `TransactionDataCache::into_effects` (~/.cargo/git/checkouts/move-5734c3a45f62af74/281f7ec/language/move-vm/runtime/src/data_cache.rs:75-126) emits `Op::Modify` for every `GlobalValue` whose status is `Dirty`, and `Dirty` is set by the field write itself (move-vm/types/src/values/values_impl.rs:279-281, 2524-2538). A write performed before an abort is therefore in the changeset.
- core/executor/src/lib.rs:2739-2757 (`absorb_vm_result!`) pushes ALL `vm_changes` into `updates` first and only then checks `$status.success`; on failure it merely sets `tx_status = "aborted"`. `updates` is returned at line 2967 and committed. Aborted-tx writes are persisted.

2) dex.move:115 is a write that sits before still-failing asserts.
core/vm_move/stdlib/sources/dex.move `add_liquidity`, fresh-pool branch:
  110 `if (pool.lp_supply == 0) {`
  114 `liquidity = raw_liquidity - MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY;`
  115 `pool.lp_supply = pool.lp_supply + MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY;`   ← global write
  136 `assert!(liquidity >= min_lp, ...)`                       ← attacker-chosen abort
  139-140 `coin::withdraw<X/Y>(account, ...)`                    ← never reached
An attacker passes `amount_x = amount_y = 10_000` (so `sqrt(x*y)=10_000 > MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY`) and `min_lp = u128::MAX`. Abort at :136 leaves `lp_supply = 1000` with `coin_x = coin_y = 0`. No tokens are needed — the withdraws are after the abort point.

3) PoC executed (executor `execute_transaction` → real Move VM → apply_updates), attacker funded with 100_000 AIN for gas and ZERO WBTC:
  `POC-RESULT status="aborted" lp_supply=1000 coin_x=0 coin_y=0`
The pre-existing test `test_dex_initial_liquidity_below_minimum_aborts_after_gas_only` (core/executor/src/lib.rs:4834) does NOT cover this: its abort is at dex.move:113, i.e. before the :115 write, so it passes while the bug is live. Same for the other dex abort tests (:4902, :4978, :5056) — all abort before any global write.

4) The corrupted state is terminal and unrecoverable on-chain:
- future `add_liquidity` takes the `else` branch (lp_supply != 0) and dies on `assert!(reserve_x > 0 && reserve_y > 0)` (dex.move:119) — forever;
- `swap_x_to_y` / `swap_y_to_x` die on the same reserve check (dex.move:208, 235);
- `remove_liquidity` is unusable: the attacker's `LPToken` is created at dex.move:146-148, after the abort point, so nobody holds LP for that pool and the 1000 `lp_supply` is stranded;
- the pair can never be re-pooled anywhere: `create_pool` rejects on `pool_exists(&registry.pools, &pool_key)` (dex.move:72) and `pool_key` is derived only from the two type names (dex.move:265-282) — it is address-independent, so a replacement pool at a different address is also blocked;
- dex.move has no admin/deactivate/reset function (`active` is only ever set true at :88), and 0x1 publishing is genesis/system-only (core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:420-422, core/executor/src/lib.rs:2883-2886), so recovery needs a coordinated stdlib upgrade + state surgery.

5) Reachability: `add_liquidity` is `public entry fun` (dex.move:93), dispatched via the normal BCS `EntryFunction` payload; the PoC drove it through `Executor::execute_transaction` exactly as a P2P/RPC tx would. Cost = gas only.

Scope correction to the claim's wording: "any pool" is slightly overbroad. Only pools in the `lp_supply == 0` state (i.e. every pool between `create_pool` and its first successful `add_liquidity`) can be bricked this way; already-seeded pools are not brickable by this path (the `else` branch writes `lp_supply` at :143 only after both withdraws succeed, and nothing aborts after it). That does not reduce severity for the launch: the ~5M AIN float pool must pass through `lp_supply == 0`, and any observer can land the bricking tx right after `create_pool`, permanently and irrecoverably blocking that pair chain-wide. Also note `create_pool` itself is squattable by anyone for any pair (dex.move:63-90 has no authorization), which pairs badly with the address-independent duplicate check. Severity CRITICAL as claimed (permanent, free, unauthenticated, unrecoverable denial of the flagship launch feature) — the impact is availability/griefing, not direct theft; no existing LP funds are stolen or frozen.

ROOT CAUSE IS BIGGER THAN DEX: committing an aborted session's changeset (vm_move/src/lib.rs:553 + executor/src/lib.rs:2741) makes EVERY Move module's asserts non-atomic — staking, governance, treasury, token_factory, delegation all inherit "partial write survives abort". dex.move:115 is just the cleanest weaponization. This should be treated as a chain-wide invariant break, not a DEX bug.
round2_verdicts.minimal_fix:
Two layers; the second is the one that actually closes the class.

(1) Chain-wide (required): never commit the changeset of an aborted payload. In core/vm_move/src/lib.rs `execute_transaction_actions`, split the sessions — run the `must_succeed == true` pre-actions (the `coin::deduct_gas` call staged at core/executor/src/lib.rs:2667-2693) in one session, `finish()` it and keep those changes; run the user payload in a SECOND session and, if it returns Err, drop that session without calling `finish()`, returning only the gas-session changes plus `ExecutionStatus::aborted(...)`. Equivalently, at lib.rs:541-556, on any action error discard `session` and re-derive the changeset from a gas-only session. The executor keeps charging gas, bumping the sequence number, and writing the "aborted" receipt exactly as today (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2739-2757 then needs `updates` from the gas session only).

(2) Defense-in-depth in dex.move: make `add_liquidity` compute-then-write — move `pool.lp_supply = pool.lp_supply + MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY;` (line 115) out of the branch and fold it into the single mutation at line 143 (e.g. `let minted_floor = if first { MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY } else { 0 };` … `pool.lp_supply = pool.lp_supply + liquidity + minted_floor;`), so every global write happens after the last `assert!` and after both `coin::withdraw` calls succeed. Apply the same "no global write before the last abort point" review to remove_liquidity/swaps and to the other stdlib modules.

Regression test: the PoC above — create_pool, then `add_liquidity(amount_x=10_000, amount_y=10_000, min_lp=u128::MAX)` from an account with zero Y — must leave `lp_supply == 0` and leave the pool tradable.

round2_verdicts.title: dex-u128-overflow
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
The claim's arithmetic assumes both pool legs are 1e18-scaled. They are not, for any pool that exists on this chain.

DECIMALS (established from source, not assumption):
- AIN = 18 decimals: `core/vm_move/stdlib/sources/staking.move:38` `MAX_SUPPLY: u128 = 150000000000000000000000000` (=150M x 1e18); `core/node/src/api_local.rs:433` returns `"decimals": 18` for AIN; `api_local.rs:1621` same; `indexer/src/main.rs:98-103` `token_decimals()` -> AIN 18.
- The only other coin on-chain is WBTC at 8 decimals: `indexer/src/main.rs:101` maps `0x1::wbtc::WBTC` -> 8; `api_local.rs:433` returns 8 for WBTC; `api_local.rs:2596` asserts it. `coin_balance()` at `api_local.rs:418-427` accepts exactly two token aliases, AIN and WBTC.
- Canonical ordering at `dex.move:272` (`bytes_lt`) makes X = `0x1::staking::AincoreCoin`, Y = `0x1::wbtc::WBTC` ("s" < "w"), matching the indexer's pair test at `indexer/src/main.rs:1349-1382`.

CLAIMED FAILURE DOES NOT OCCUR. The initial-seed path is `dex.move:110-117`: `assert_mul_safe(amount_x, amount_y)` then `sqrt(amount_x * amount_y)`. `assert_mul_safe` (`dex.move:322-326`) requires `b <= (2^128-1)/a`. With amount_x = 5,000,000 AIN = 5.0e24 base units, the permitted Y side is up to 3.4028e38/5.0e24 = 6.806e13 base units = **680,564 BTC**. Seeding the entire 5M AIN float against any realistic BTC amount passes with ~4 orders of magnitude of headroom. Even the full 150M cap (1.5e26) permits 22,685 BTC on the other leg. `sqrt` at `dex.move:346` operates on the already-bounded product. So "the DEX cannot hold the 5M AIN float AT ALL" is false — the seed transaction succeeds.

Swaps also pass at launch scale. `quote_out` (`dex.move:310-320`): the tightest guard is `assert_mul_safe(amount_in_with_fee, reserve_out)` at :315, i.e. `amount_in * 9970 * reserve_out <= 2^128-1`. With reserve_out = 5e24 AIN, a BTC-in swap is capped at 6.826e9 base = **68.3 BTC per swap** — larger than any plausible pool depth at launch (68x a 1-BTC pool, 1.4x a 50-BTC pool). AIN-in swaps against a 100-BTC leg are capped at 3.4e24 base = 3.4M AIN. `assert_mul_safe(reserve_in, BPS_DENOMINATOR)` at :316 caps reserve_in at 3.4e34, far above the 1.5e26 supply cap. Not binding.

WHAT IS REAL (narrower, and not what was claimed). The un-widened mulDiv does bite on the *non-first* liquidity paths, because the intermediate is `amount * lp_supply` rather than `amount_x * amount_y`:
- `dex.move:120-121` `assert_mul_safe(amount_x, pool.lp_supply)` and `:129-130` `assert_mul_safe(liquidity, reserve_x)`. With lp_supply = sqrt(R_x*R_y), the per-transaction cap is f <= MAX/(R_x * L). For a 5M AIN / 100 BTC pool (L = 2.24e17), a subsequent `add_liquidity` aborts with EOVERFLOW (=4, `dex.move:15`) above ~1.52e21 base = **~1,522 AIN, i.e. 0.030% of the reserve, per call**. For a 5M AIN / 1 BTC pool the cap is ~15,218 AIN (0.30%).
- `dex.move:174-175` imposes the mirror limit on exit: `lp_amount <= MAX/reserve_x` = 6.81e13 out of an L of 2.24e17, i.e. **0.030% of LP supply per call**. Withdrawing the founder's full seed position would take ~3,300 transactions.
- A hypothetical 18-dec/18-dec pool (creatable, since `token_factory.move:77` permits `decimals <= 18` and `dex.move:63` `create_pool` is permissionless) is genuinely unusable: the initial-seed guard caps the geometric mean of the two deposits at sqrt(2^128-1) = **18.45 tokens**. No such pool is canonical today (only AIN and WBTC are recognized, `api_local.rs:418-427`).

Severity honesty: all of these are fail-closed aborts via `assert_mul_safe` before the multiply — a clean EOVERFLOW revert, never a wrapped/truncated value, so there is no fund loss, no mispricing, and no theft primitive. I checked for a funds-lock case: exit is stuck only if `L/min(R) > MAX/max(R)`, which for an 8-dec BTC leg needs an AIN reserve above 2.26e28 base = 22.6 billion AIN, unreachable under the 150M cap. So funds are always retrievable, just in many chunks. This is a functional/liquidity-management defect (LOW as a security finding), not the HIGH "DEX can't hold the float" blocker asserted.

round2_verdicts.title: epoch-noauth
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
Empirically confirmed with a live end-to-end test through the real block path, but the claim's stated impact is only half right.

SOURCE FACTS
- core/vm_move/stdlib/sources/epoch.move:26 — `public entry fun advance_epoch(account: &signer)`. No `assert!(signer::address_of(account) == @0x1)`. Compare epoch.move:41-48 (`update_epoch_duration`) which DOES assert `addr == @0x1`.
- epoch.move:28,32 — the resource is mutated FIRST (`epoch_number + 1`, `epoch_start_time + epoch_duration`), and only AFTER that does it call `staking::cleanup_old_unbonding(account)` (:35) and `staking::distribute_rewards(account)` (:38).
- staking.move:255-257 and :366-369 both assert `addr == @0x1` (`error::permission_denied(ENOT_VALIDATOR)`), so a user-signer call DOES abort at cleanup_old_unbonding.
- core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:565-612 `bind_signer_args` overwrites every leading `&signer` slot with the authenticated sender, so a forged @0x1 in the payload is discarded (executor lib.rs:2817-2821 passes `sender_addr` as auth_signer). So the attacker cannot obtain a 0x1 signer — distribute_rewards never runs.

WHY IT IS STILL EXPLOITABLE (the claim's "verify" hint about distribute_rewards is the wrong shield)
The abort does NOT roll back the mutation. core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:472-556 runs all actions in ONE session; on a non-`must_succeed` failure it only records `status = aborted` (:541-550) and then still calls `session.finish()` (:553) and returns the changeset. In move-vm aptos-v1.3.0, `borrow_global_mut` + `write_ref` marks the cached global Dirty (values_impl.rs:279-283) and `into_effect` emits `Op::Modify` for Dirty cached globals (values_impl.rs:2531-2536) regardless of abort — the VM relies on the adapter discarding the session, which AINCORE does not do. Then core/executor/src/lib.rs:2739-2757 (`absorb_vm_result!`) pushes `vm_changes` into `updates` UNCONDITIONALLY and only afterwards flags `tx_status = "aborted"`, and lib.rs:2959-2967 returns those updates for commit. The "⚠️ Payload execution failed (state reverted)" log at vm_move/src/lib.rs:545 is false.

EMPIRICAL PROOF (temporary test added to core/executor/src/lib.rs tests, run, then reverted via git checkout)
Seeded `resource_0x1..01_0x1::epoch::Epoch = (5, 1000, 777)`, submitted a normally-signed user tx (non-0x1 account, forged @0x1 arg bytes) calling `0x1::epoch::advance_epoch` through `execute_block_parallel`. Output: abort at `staking::cleanup_old_unbonding` sub status 327681, gas charged — and the DB afterwards read `epoch_number=6 epoch_start_time=1777`. The clock moved on an aborted user tx.

REACHABILITY: core/mempool/src/lib.rs:291-298 applies no module allowlist to EntryFunction payloads (only join_validator_set PoP and Script-disabled), so any funded account can submit this. Every node applies the same partial write deterministically, so this is state corruption, not a fork.

REAL IMPACT (severity correction)
- REFUTED part of the claim: no "repeated emission distribution", no inflation — distribute_rewards aborts before minting anything.
- CONFIRMED part: `epoch::now_seconds()` (epoch.move:54) is the chain's virtual clock, consumed by delegation.move:249 (`unlock_time = now + UNBONDING_PERIOD`, 1_814_400s, delegation.move:49), :263 (`withdraw_unbonded` maturity check), :344/:356 (COMMISSION_CHANGE_DELAY 604_800s), and by core/executor/src/lib.rs:1237-1252 `on_chain_epoch_clock_secs` → `drive_governance` (lib.rs:1176, :3468-3479) which executes queued governance proposals (UpdateFederationKey / UpdateEconomicParams) once `now_secs >= execution_time`. An attacker fast-forwards the clock at +`epoch_duration` per tx (genesis.json `epoch_duration = 10`, epoch.move:22) and thereby bypasses the 21-day unbonding window (the slashing window), the 7-day commission-change delay, and governance timelocks.
- Cost is linear spam: ~181k txs for the full unbonding period, ~60k for the commission delay, fewer for a shorter governance timelock; gas is charged on each. Real but not free, and no direct mint or fund theft — hence HIGH, not CRITICAL.

BROADER FINDING (worth its own item): the partial-write-on-abort behavior in `absorb_vm_result!` is generic — ANY 0x1 entry function that mutates state before a later authorization/validation abort leaks those mutations into committed state. epoch::advance_epoch is just the instance with the sharpest teeth. This should be re-swept across the stdlib before mainnet/DEX activation.

round2_verdicts.title: blockhash-walltime
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
The timestamp is LOCALLY RECOMPUTED on every committing node, not author-set-and-replicated. Proof chain from source: (1) consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:56-59 — Block::new_with_roots calls SystemTime::now() internally; there is no timestamp parameter, so no caller can supply an author value. (2) consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:104 — calculate_header_hash folds header.timestamp into the digest. (3) consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:911 — the ONLY production call site: every validator that passes the observer guard independently builds its own Block from its own commit sequence. Blocks are never gossiped in the commit path (only Vertex is — dag.rs:429/703); the only replicated block path is chain sync, which serves the producer's stored JSON. (4) consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:920 — latest_block_hash = new_block.header.hash and feeds the next block's prev_hash (dag.rs:914), so one mismatch diverges the block-hash chain permanently. Note the Vertex timestamp (blockchain/src/lib.rs:126) IS author-set, signed and hash-bound (verified at dag.rs:703, drift-bounded at dag.rs:659-677) — vertices are fine; only blocks are locally re-derived.

WHY THE EMPIRICAL LOCKSTEP EVIDENCE IS VOID: genesis.json contains exactly ONE validator (n=1). dag.rs:830 returns early for any node not in the validator set ("Observer Mode: skipping local ordering/commit"), so on the live 3-node cluster only a single node ever reaches dag.rs:911. There has never been a second block producer to disagree with; 349k rounds of "identical digests" is evidence about state_root/finality_digest, not about block-header hashes.

BUT SEVERITY IS INFLATED — this is not CRITICAL. It does NOT diverge state: state_root/receipts_root are computed by executor.execute_block_parallel BEFORE the block is constructed (dag.rs:900-919) and the executor never consumes a block hash (grep of core/executor/src/lib.rs for block_hash: no hits). It does NOT halt consensus: DAG ordering/commit never reads block.header.hash. It does NOT fork leader election: ordering.rs:692-707 deliberately elects from the deterministic step1_beacon, not the QC-folded last_vdf_output, precisely to kill that class of timing divergence.

REAL IMPACT, reachable with zero Byzantine participants as soon as a second validator commits (the intended n>=4 mainnet topology): (a) Multi-party QC finality certificates break. qc.rs:40-54 — FinalityVote carries block_hash and "All validators MUST sign byte-identical bytes for fast_aggregate_verify"; qc_producer.rs:353-357 drops any peer vote whose block_hash differs, and even with expected_block_hash=None the BLS aggregate over differing messages cannot verify (qc.rs:303-309). Aggregation therefore succeeds only in the coincidence where all validators commit inside the same UNIX second. QC is the stated finality root for light clients and bridge finality proofs (qc.rs:6-9) — directly load-bearing for the DEX/bridge launch. (b) Cross-validator block continuity breaks: sync/src/lib.rs:264 rejects on prev_hash mismatch, so a restarted validator cannot sequentially sync from a peer whose locally-built chain used different timestamps (dag.rs:828-829 already acknowledges this failure mode for observers). (c) Accumulator root (dag.rs:923) and DA batch identity (dag.rs:978) are keyed on the divergent hash, and aincore block-hash RPC answers differ per node.

REINFORCING DEFECT AT THE SAME SITE: dag.rs:913 passes vertex.round — the round of whichever incoming vertex happened to trigger the local commit — instead of the deterministic commit.anchor_round (which is available and is what the QC context uses at dag.rs:1009-1010). self.latest_block_height (dag.rs:910) is likewise a local counter. So fixing the timestamp alone is necessary but not sufficient to make the header canonical.
round2_verdicts.minimal_fix: Make the block header a pure function of committed consensus data. In consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs, add a timestamp parameter to new_with_roots (e.g. new_with_roots_at(..., timestamp: u64)) instead of calling SystemTime::now() at line 56, keeping the existing constructor as a thin wrapper for tests. At consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:911, pass a timestamp derived from the committed vertices themselves — the max (or median) of the `timestamp` fields of the vertices in commit.sequence, which are author-set, Ed25519-signed, hash-bound (verified at dag.rs:703) and future-drift-bounded (dag.rs:659-677), hence identical on every node. In the same call, replace `vertex.round` (dag.rs:913) with `commit.anchor_round`. Add a determinism test that builds the same commit sequence twice with different wall clocks and asserts an identical header hash. This is a block-format change: it must land before mainnet genesis, or behind an explicit height/epoch activation, since it changes every header hash.

round2_verdicts.title: slash-nodelocal
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
Both halves of the claim check out against source, and the claim is a DISTINCT root cause from finding #3.

(1) The slash trigger is gossip-arrival-timed, not ordered-block-derived.
- Equivocation: `dag.rs:1351 apply_equivocation_slash()` writes `sys:pending_slash:{offender}` (dag.rs:1381-1384) plus `validator:jailed:{offender}` the instant a proof is seen. It is reached from local detection in `add_vertex` (dag.rs:772) AND from inbound gossip `EQUIV_PROOF:` → `handle_remote_equivocation` (dag.rs:1589 dispatch, dag.rs:1476 apply). Nothing binds it to a committed round/height.
- Downtime: `dag.rs:533` writes a local attestation, `dag.rs:1585` ingests remote `DOWNTIME_ATTEST:` and stores them (dag.rs:1738-1760). `executor lib.rs:1790 promote_downtime_attestations_to_slash()` promotes to `sys:pending_slash:` the moment the locally-held attestation set crosses stake quorum — i.e. when the Nth attestation gossip lands.
- Drain: `execute_block_parallel` calls `promote_downtime_attestations_to_slash()` (lib.rs:1738) then `execute_pending_slashes()` (lib.rs:1743) at the end of whatever block that node is currently executing. `execute_pending_slashes` scans the KV prefix (lib.rs:1934) with no height/round gate. So node A applies the slash at height H, node B at H+k where k is pure network timing. Every node executes blocks locally (dag.rs:901 on the consensus path, sync/src/lib.rs:975 on the sync path), so both paths drain their own arrival-timed queue.

(2) The resulting state writes are genuinely outside the state root.
`sys:state_root` is a running hash updated ONLY inside the per-batch tx loop: `batch_hasher` absorbs only tx write-sets (lib.rs:1598-1616) and `write_batch.put("sys:state_root", ...)` at lib.rs:1631. `execute_pending_slashes` runs after that loop and writes straight to the DB, bypassing both hasher and batch: Move VM slash changes at lib.rs:2015-2020, delegation slash changes at lib.rs:2055-2060, `sys:validators` rewrite at lib.rs:2087-2115, `sys:validator_set:v1` prune at lib.rs:2119-2144, tombstone at lib.rs:2147. `summary.state_root` at lib.rs:1750 just re-reads `sys:state_root` (lib.rs:951-957), which the slash never touched. On an empty block (the live testnet's actual state) there are no batches at all, so the root does not move even though the slash mutated stake, supply and the validator set.

Consequences, and why they are not caught: the state root is consensus-critical everywhere else — it is hashed into the block header (consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:98-99), carried in the QC finality vote (dag.rs:905, qc.rs:50/80), and compared on sync (sync/src/lib.rs:120). Because slash writes are excluded, that entire detection layer is blind to this class of divergence. Two concrete divergences follow:
- Permanent economic divergence: the slash burns a percentage of *current* bonded stake (`slash_validator_bps` with `slash_pct*100` bps, lib.rs:1978-2007; `delegation::slash_pool` lib.rs:2035-2050). Rewards are distributed at a deterministic epoch interval by `maybe_advance_epoch` (lib.rs:1747). A node that applies a 5% downtime slash before the epoch advance and one that applies it after burn different absolute amounts, then both write the tombstone `sys:slashed:{addr}:{round}` (lib.rs:2147) and never retry. `sync_supply_trackers_from_validator_set` (lib.rs:2021) propagates that into `sys:total_supply`. Divergent supply, matching roots, no alarm.
- Transient consensus-set divergence at the worst possible moment: the slash strips the validator from `sys:validators` and from the authoritative QC trust root `sys:validator_set:v1` (lib.rs:2119-2136). For the k blocks between node A's and node B's application, the two nodes compute stake-weighted quorum over different sets, so a QC valid on one is invalid on the other — and a Byzantine validator controls the timing, since it chooses when and to whom it gossips the conflicting vertices.

Adversarial checks: (a) no guard exists — the dedup guards (`sys:equiv_seen` dag.rs:1357, tombstone lib.rs:2091) make the slash exactly-once per node but say nothing about *which height* it lands at; (b) not already fixed — HEAD d5df123 still has the arrival-timed queue and the root-bypassing writes; (c) reachable on real entry points — the equivocation path needs a validator that double-signs (the exact scenario the code exists to punish, attacker-controlled); the downtime path needs no attacker at all, just one validator offline for DOWNTIME_THRESHOLD rounds while the rest reach stake quorum, which this deployment has already experienced.

Distinct from finding #3: #3 is about which vertices fall in which committed partition. This is a state mutation that is not derived from ordered content in any form — fixing ordering determinism leaves it fully intact.

Severity honesty: down-rating CRITICAL → HIGH. It is real, reachable and produces silent unrecoverable state divergence, but it needs a slash event to actually fire (none has on the live cluster, which is exactly why supply/digest still match across the three nodes), and it yields no direct mint/theft primitive for the attacker — unlike the confirmed CRITICAL at lib.rs:2307. It is squarely in the same band as the confirmed ordering/fork HIGHs, and it is a mainnet blocker before the DEX float goes live.
round2_verdicts.minimal_fix:
Two changes, both needed:
1. Make the apply height deterministic. Stop draining `sys:pending_slash:` on arrival. Record the evidence with its consensus round (already present in the slash event, lib.rs:1946) and gate `execute_pending_slashes` on a fixed, chain-derived deadline: only execute a pending slash when the block being executed maps to round >= evidence_round + D (D = a fixed grace window comfortably above gossip latency), and drop any slash whose evidence arrives after its deadline (it will be re-gossiped and picked up in a later window). Every honest node then applies the identical slash at the identical height regardless of when the proof reached it. Same gate for `promote_downtime_attestations_to_slash`: freeze the attestation set at the epoch boundary (the `epoch` already in the key, lib.rs:1908) and promote only at a fixed height offset from that boundary. The durable fix is to carry the proof as an ordered system transaction in the block payload, but the deadline gate is the smallest correct version.
2. Put slash writes in the state root. Route every write in `execute_pending_slashes` (lib.rs:2015-2020, 2055-2060, 2087-2115, 2119-2144, 2147) through the same `WriteBatch` + `batch_hasher` that feeds `sys:state_root` at lib.rs:1616-1631, so any remaining divergence is detected by the QC vote (dag.rs:905) and the sync check (sync/src/lib.rs:120) instead of persisting silently. Note this makes the root move on empty blocks too, which is correct — the state did change.

round2_verdicts.title: stateroot-coverage
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
The factual claim is accurate and, if anything, understated.

WHAT THE ROOT COVERS. core/executor/src/lib.rs:1594-1639 is the only place sys:state_root is ever written (grep across the workspace returns exactly executor 1622 read / 1631 write, plus the 953 reader). It sits INSIDE the `for batch in batches.iter()` tx loop: 1599-1615 hash only the (key,value) updates returned by execute_transaction; 1622-1628 fold them as new_root = SHA256(prev_root || batch_hash); 1631 persists it. It is a running hash-chain over the transaction write stream, not a state commitment.

WHAT IS EXCLUDED. Every settlement write in steps 5-8 of execute_block_parallel lands outside that loop and is never hashed:
- 1668 burn_supply_trackers -> raw self.db.put at 1280 (total_burned), 1288-1290 (sys:total_supply), 1299 (ValidatorSet), 1328 (SupplyStats)
- 1709 deposit_fee_reward -> raw db.put/db.delete of every Move VM change at 1443-1444 (miner CoinStore)
- 1725 queue_fee_sweep -> db.put at 1468
- 1743 execute_pending_slashes -> db.put of vm_changes at ~2015
- 1747 maybe_advance_epoch -> commit_kv_updates at 1166; commit_kv_updates (1029-1046) builds a WriteBatch with NO hashing whatsoever. This is the epoch emission path, i.e. the entire 150M issuance.
- 1171 rotate_validator_epoch and 1176 drive_governance (on-chain governance execution) likewise use raw puts.
summary.state_root at 1750 simply re-reads sys:state_root, so it reflects the last tx batch only.

WORSE THAN CLAIMED. schedule_batches (2357-2395) returns an empty Vec when parsed_txs is empty, so with zero transactions the batch loop never executes and sys:state_root is not touched at all. On the live heartbeat-only testnet (~349k rounds, empty payloads) the root has never moved off the genesis default while emission, fee payout and slashing have been mutating balances continuously.

DOES ANY CONSENSUS CHECK DEPEND ON IT? Yes, two, so this is not cosmetic:
(1) consensus/consensus/src/qc.rs:50 puts state_root in FinalityVote, and to_signing_bytes (60-66) BCS-serializes the whole struct; BLS fast_aggregate_verify requires byte-identical messages, so a state_root divergence would prevent multi-party QC formation. It can never do so for any excluded write.
(2) sync/src/lib.rs:120 verify_execution_roots rejects a block whose header state_root differs from the locally recomputed one. For empty blocks this compares a constant against a constant, so the AINCORE_REQUIRE_EXEC_ROOTS cutover control (sync/src/lib.rs:106-119) is largely hollow in the current regime.

SEVERITY, HONESTLY (HIGH -> MEDIUM). There is no attacker-controlled entry point that reaches this; it is a missing-invariant / detection gap, not an exploit primitive — nobody mints or steals because of it. A state root also only catches divergence, not invalidity: with full coverage it still would not have caught confirmed CRITICAL #1, since all nodes running the same code mint the same wrong amount. What keeps it above LOW is that divergence is reachable with no attacker at all: maybe_advance_epoch silently returns on Move abort (1163) or VM error (1180), and deposit_fee_reward falls back to node-local queue_fee_sweep after 3 failed attempts (1724-1727). A node that skips one epoch emission, or queues instead of paying, diverges in supply and balances permanently, and neither the QC path nor the sync root check can detect it. With the DEX live against the ~5M float that shows up as RPC nodes serving different balances while both report finality.

CAVEAT FOR THE FIX. sys:pending_slash:* and sys:fee_sweep_queue:* are written from node-local observation, and the drain caps in execute_pending_slashes (5) and process_fee_sweep_queue (25) depend on local queue contents. Folding those into the root as-is converts today's silent divergence into a hard chain halt, so they must be made deterministic first or explicitly excluded with the exclusion documented, the way rotate_validator_epoch's comment at 1192-1194 already does for consensus metadata.
round2_verdicts.minimal_fix:
Make the accumulator cover post-batch settlement, in this order:

1. Extract the fold from the tx loop into one helper on Executor:
   fn commit_and_fold(&self, mut updates: Vec<(String, Option<String>)>, context: &str) -> Result<(), String>
   Sort updates by key, build a WriteBatch, and hash each (key, value) / (key, b"DELETE") pair into a batch_hasher exactly as lines 1601-1612 do; then read sys:state_root, fold new_root = SHA256(prev_root || batch_hash), put sys:state_root into the same WriteBatch, and write once. Have the tx loop at 1594-1639 call it so there is a single implementation.

2. Route the deterministic settlement writers through it instead of raw db.put:
   - commit_kv_updates (1029-1046) -> delegate to commit_and_fold (this covers maybe_advance_epoch/emission at 1166).
   - deposit_fee_reward (1441-1446) -> collect vm_changes into a Vec and commit_and_fold them.
   - execute_pending_slashes (~2014-2016) -> same for its vm_changes.
   - burn_supply_trackers (1280, 1288, 1299, 1328) -> accumulate the four writes into one Vec and commit_and_fold once.

3. Do NOT fold node-local queues/metadata: sys:fee_sweep_queue:*, sys:pending_slash:*, sys:downtime_attestation:*, consensus:* and sys:validator_set:epoch:*. Keep them on raw put and add a comment naming them as deliberately out-of-root (mirroring the note at 1192-1194), otherwise the fix turns existing per-node queue divergence into a chain halt.

4. Kill the constant-root case for empty blocks: seed the fold once per block with the block height (and proposer) even when batches is empty, e.g. call commit_and_fold with an empty update set after step 8 so every block advances the root. Then AINCORE_REQUIRE_EXEC_ROOTS actually binds a header to executed state.

5. Add a test that executes two blocks with identical (empty) tx sets but different epoch-advance outcomes and asserts the resulting state_root values differ.

round2_verdicts.title: mempool-failopen
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
Both halves of the claim check out in source, though the causal attribution needs correcting.

(1) The admission gate IS fail-open, exactly as claimed. core/mempool/src/lib.rs:216-233 wraps the balance check in nested `if let Some(...)`: `executor::committed_ain_balance(storage, &sender)` returning `None` falls through to admission with no rejection. core/executor/src/lib.rs:81-93 returns `None` on missing CoinStore resource key (`db.get(&key).ok().flatten()?`, line 90), unparseable address (line 82), or corrupt BCS (line 92) — and the repo's own test at core/executor/src/lib.rs:3558-3575 (`committed_ain_balance_reads_store_and_fails_open`) asserts `None` for a missing store. So a freshly generated keypair with no CoinStore is ALWAYS admitted. Second fail-open branch: `checked_mul` at lib.rs:218-220 — on overflow the whole check is skipped, so `gas_price = u128::MAX` with `gas_limit >= 2` is admitted unchecked. Signature verification (lib.rs:426-472) still passes because the attacker signs his own txs.

(2) There is NO byte cap anywhere between the per-tx limit and the transport limit. Mempool allows 100 KB per tx (lib.rs:169-177). consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:419 pulls `get_pending_transactions(50)` — a COUNT limit only, no cumulative byte accounting (same at consensus/consensus/src/lib.rs:159). The vertex is then JSON-serialized whole at dag.rs:1158. Worst case 50 x 100 KB ~= 5 MB; the threshold is crossed at ~11 txs.

(3) Both transports hard-cap at 1 MiB, so such a vertex cannot propagate: gossipsub `max_transmit_size(1 << 20)` at core/node/src/p2p.rs:114, and the TCP frame guard `if msg_len > 1024 * 1024 { break }` at common/network/src/lib.rs:239 (which also kills the connection). dag.rs:1168-1193 ignores the send result in both branches — no error surfaces.

(4) The proposer has ALREADY inserted the vertex into its own DAG (dag.rs:447) before the failed broadcast, and get_pending_transactions drains the txs from the mempool (lib.rs:589-598). There is no missing-vertex repair path — grep for orphan/missing_parent/pending_vertices/REQUEST_VERTEX across consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs returns nothing.

(5) Halt is real, not theoretical. Parent quorum at dag.rs:360-379 is stake-weighted via `qc::stake_quorum_met` (consensus/consensus/src/qc.rs:194-196: `signed*3 > total*2`, STRICT). With the live 3-validator equal-stake set, 2 of 3 gives 2*3 = 6 which is not > 3*2 = 6, so all three round-N vertices are required. One proposer's vertex failing to propagate permanently stalls the other two; the proposer then stalls one round later for lack of round-N+1 parents. This generalizes to any n: the attacker simply submits ~11 oversized txs to EVERY validator's RPC, so no proposer's vertex propagates.

(6) Reachability is trivial and unauthenticated. `aincore_sendTransaction` is a public JSON-RPC method (core/node/src/api.rs:148-173) bound to 0.0.0.0 (api.rs:619); rate limiter is burst 200 (api.rs:586-590), and only ~11 requests per validator are needed. Payload is a BCS EntryFunction with one large `vector<u8>` arg — decodes fine at mempool lib.rs:290-298, and verify_join_validator_pop_mempool (lib.rs:22-27) returns Ok for any non-`0x1::staking` module.

CORRECTIONS to the claim's framing: the fail-open balance gate is an AMPLIFIER, not the root cause. Even fail-closed, the gate only requires `balance >= gas_limit * gas_price`, so `gas_limit=1, gas_price=1` costs 1 quanta — near-free either way. The root defect is the missing cumulative byte cap at dag.rs:419. That makes it worse than claimed: 11 legitimate 100 KB txs from a funded user trigger the same permanent halt with no attacker at all. Separately, the overflow fail-open composes badly with the fee-market selector at mempool lib.rs:557-572 (gas_price DESC): an attacker with zero balance and `gas_price = u128::MAX` is admitted AND wins every one of the 50 slots ahead of all paying users, permanently.

Severity CRITICAL is honest here: remote, unauthenticated, zero-cost, permanent unrecoverable chain halt with no repair path — and accidentally triggerable by honest load once the DEX makes payloads non-empty (today's testnet only survives because payloads are empty heartbeats).
round2_verdicts.minimal_fix:
Two changes, both small:

1. PRIMARY (fixes the halt): add a cumulative byte budget to vertex payload selection. Change `Mempool::get_pending_transactions(&mut self, limit: usize)` (core/mempool/src/lib.rs:519) to `get_pending_transactions(&mut self, limit: usize, max_bytes: usize)`, and in the selection loop at lib.rs:557-585 track `bytes_used += raws[idx].len() + 8` (JSON array overhead) and `break` before pushing an index that would exceed `max_bytes`. Call it with a budget well under the 1 MiB transport cap at consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:419 and consensus/consensus/src/lib.rs:159, e.g. `get_pending_transactions(50, 512 * 1024)`. Belt-and-braces: in `broadcast_vertex` (dag.rs:1158-1165) check `serialized.len() >= 1 << 20` and refuse to build/emit, logging loudly, rather than silently forking the local DAG.

2. SECONDARY (removes the zero-cost + priority-monopoly amplifier): make the two fail-open branches at core/mempool/src/lib.rs:216-233 fail CLOSED. Reject when `checked_mul` returns None ("gas_limit x gas_price overflows"), and reject when `committed_ain_balance` returns None AND the sender has no pending-nonce entry in this mempool (so a genuinely new account funded by an earlier same-block tx is still admitted, but an account with no CoinStore and no in-flight funding tx is not). Optionally also cap gas_price at a sane ceiling so the fee-market selector at lib.rs:557-572 cannot be monopolized.

round2_verdicts.title: mempool-gasauction
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
The claim's literal premise ("no funding check") is WRONG — a funding gate exists at core/mempool/src/lib.rs:216-233 (SEC-#27), and production wires it (core/node/src/main.rs:545 uses `Mempool::with_storage`; the `Mempool::new()` call sites in api_local.rs:2452+ are all under `#[cfg(test)]` at api_local.rs:2427). But the gate is fail-open in exactly the attacker's case, so the exploit and impact survive intact.

MECHANISM (corrected):
1. Ordering IS by attacker-declared gas_price. core/mempool/src/lib.rs:557-572 loops `limit` times picking the highest-gas_price per-sender head (`gp > *bgp`), tie-broken by FIFO index. Nothing in that loop consults balance.
2. The admission gate calls `executor::committed_ain_balance` (core/executor/src/lib.rs:81-93), which reads `resource_{addr}_0x1::coin::CoinStore<0x1::staking::AincoreCoin>` and returns `None` when the key is absent (lib.rs:90 `db.get(&key).ok().flatten()?`). The mempool treats `None` as "unknown → admit" (lib.rs:221-230: the reject only fires inside `if let Some(balance)`). A never-funded address has no CoinStore resource, so it returns `None` and is admitted with an arbitrary gas_price. The gate therefore blocks a sender holding 1 AIN who declares a huge gas_price, but admits a sender holding nothing. The docstring at executor/src/lib.rs:75-80 states this fail-open intent explicitly.
3. The attack is free. At core/executor/src/lib.rs:2450 `let sender_obj = self.db.get_object(&tx.sender)?;` — inside an Option-returning closure, so a nonexistent sender account returns `None` and the tx is dropped before the sequence check (2557), before `deduct_gas` (2684-2693), and before any nonce increment (2703). No gas charged, no state written. The attacker pays nothing and can recycle indefinitely (canonical-hash dedup at lib.rs:247 is evaded with fresh seq numbers or fresh keypairs).
4. Blast radius is total, not partial: a vertex payload is only 50 txs (consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:419 and consensus/consensus/src/lib.rs:159 both call `get_pending_transactions(50)`). ~50 in-flight max-gas_price txs occupy 100% of every block. A single sender suffices — the selection loop advances that sender's cursor and re-picks it every iteration since it still holds the top price. Secondary effect: MAX_PENDING_TXS = 5000 (lib.rs:73, enforced at 484-490) means the attacker can also fill the queue outright, turning ordering censorship into a flat "Mempool full" admission DoS for everyone.

REACHABILITY (real, attacker-controlled, two paths):
- JSON-RPC: core/node/src/api.rs:165 `mempool.add_transaction(tx_str)`. Rate-limited per-IP at api.rs:586-588 (`per_second(100)`/`burst_size(200)` = burst 200 then 1 per 100s), which alone would blunt this.
- P2P `TX:` inbound: core/node/src/main.rs:671 (gossip) and main.rs:714-721 (TCP server). This path has NO governor. The TCP handshake at common/network/src/lib.rs:153-198 has the server sign but never verifies any client identity — the client sends only a 32-byte ephemeral key — so any anonymous peer connects, and the only throttle is the ~100 msg/s per-connection cap at common/network/src/lib.rs:207, well above the ~50 tx/round needed. The RPC rate limiter does not save this.
gas_price is bound into the signed message (lib.rs:409-418, 448-457), but the attacker signs with their own key, so it is fully attacker-controlled.

SEVERITY: HIGH is honest, not inflated. It is a free, sustained, unattributable censorship / liveness DoS on the entire transaction path — directly fatal to the DEX activation, since all trades against the ~5M AIN float can be frozen at zero cost. It is NOT CRITICAL: no fund loss, no inflation, no consensus-safety or state-divergence break, and it is recoverable by patching and restarting rather than by a fork.

NOT already fixed at HEAD d5df123, and no guard, type property, or friend restriction prevents it: there is no account-existence check anywhere in `add_transaction` (I read the full path, lib.rs:167-517).

round2_verdicts.title: token-factory-fee-destroy
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
Confirmed by reading source AND by executing a runtime PoC against the real Move VM.

1) TokenRegistry is never created. `core/node/src/genesis.rs` seeds exactly seven system resources — ValidatorSet (genesis.rs:969), Epoch (:998), GovernanceState (:1031), DeviceRegistry (:1071), OracleConfig (:1095), Treasury (:1117), dex::PoolRegistry (:1139). `grep -in "token" core/node/src/genesis.rs` returns only DEX `token_x_name`/`token_y_name` fields. No `0x1::token_factory::TokenRegistry` write anywhere in the repo outside test helpers (`core/executor/src/lib.rs:3824-3828` is a #[cfg(test)] key helper, and the existing test at :5238 has to hand-seed `db.put(&token_registry_key(), "00")` — which is itself evidence genesis does not).

2) It can never be created later either. `token_factory.move:56 public fun initialize(admin: &signer)` is NOT `public entry`. The executor only dispatches `MoveAction::CallEntryFunction` → `session.execute_entry_function` (core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:528), which enforces `check_is_entry` (move-vm runtime.rs:408-427). And user txs cannot publish to 0x1 (executor lib.rs:2877). So the registry is permanently unreachable — token_factory is dead code on any chain launched from this genesis, and `mint`, `burn`, `disable_minting`, `get_token_info` are all bricked too (all `borrow_global_mut<TokenRegistry>(@0x1)`).

3) The abort is AFTER the burn. `token_factory.move:86` `coin::withdraw<AincoreCoin>(creator, 100 AIN)` mutates CoinStore (coin.move:74 `store.coin.value = store.coin.value - amount`); `:87` `staking::burn_ain(fee)` mutates ValidatorSet.total_supply (staking.move:537) and SupplyStats (:544). The registry borrow is at `:98`, twelve lines later.

4) Aborts are NOT atomic in this executor — the claim's own escape hatch does not hold. `core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:472` opens ONE session; on a non-must_succeed action failure the error is only recorded into `status` (:541-551, with a misleading `"state reverted"` println at :545) and `session.finish()` runs unconditionally at :553. The executor's `absorb_vm_result!` macro (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2739-2756) pushes every vm_change into `updates` regardless of `status.success`. move-vm's `Interpreter::entrypoint` writes straight into the TransactionDataCache with no snapshot (runtime.rs:358).

5) Runtime proof. The repo's own committed PoC `zzz_audit_poc_dex_brick_partial_write` (core/executor/src/lib.rs:4981) FAILS today: `POC-RESULT status="aborted" lp_supply=1000 coin_x=0 coin_y=0` — an aborted add_liquidity leaked state.
