I then added a temporary test replicating create_token with NO seeded registry (reverted afterwards; `git status` clean) and got:
  `MISSING_DATA at Module 0x1::token_factory ... code offset 46`
  `status="aborted" balance_after=99999999999999990000 total_supply=Some("100000000000000000000") total_burned=Some("100000000000000000000") registry=None`
Starting balance was 200 AIN. After the aborted call: 100 AIN gone (fee) plus 10,000 gas units, `sys:total_supply` permanently cut from 200 to 100 AIN, `total_burned` = 100 AIN, and registry still absent. The user got nothing.

6) Reachable via a real entry point with attacker/user-controlled input: `token_factory.move:64 public entry fun create_token` and the wrapper `scripts.move:6 public entry fun create_token`. The mempool accepts EntryFunction payloads, and `core/node/src/api_local.rs:666` already ships a gas estimate for `("token_factory","create_token") => 100_000`, i.e. the RPC/wallet surface advertises it. Any user with 100 AIN can burn it, repeatedly, 100% of the time.

Severity: HIGH is honest, not inflated. It is real, permanent, unrecoverable value destruction (100 AIN + gas per call, plus a matching permanent reduction of circulating supply) on a public, RPC-advertised entry point with a 100% failure rate, and there is no on-chain remedy — fixing it requires a new genesis or a coordinated 0x1 stdlib/state migration. It is not CRITICAL: no theft, no inflation, no consensus divergence, no halt, and the loss is self-inflicted rather than attacker-forced. Given the founder is about to launch mainnet plus a DEX where "launch your own token" is exactly the feature users will click, this is a launch blocker.

Independent finding worth escalating separately: item 4 (non-atomic Move aborts committing partial state) is a general executor-level defect, not specific to token_factory. The repo's own dex PoC at core/executor/src/lib.rs:4981 is currently a failing test proving it, and it makes EVERY assert-after-mutation in the Move stdlib a potential state-corruption bug (dex.move:114 leaks `lp_supply` before the `min_lp` check at :134, bricking a pool with zero reserves).

round2_verdicts.title: governance-escrow-sink
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
Both halves of the claim hold, though "unreachable" is conditionally rather than universally true.

(1) The ENTIRE liquid balance is escrowed, not a user-chosen weight. governance.move:86-88 computes `available = coin::balance<AincoreCoin>(addr)` then `weight = available - VOTE_GAS_RESERVE` (VOTE_GAS_RESERVE = 1 AIN, line 14). `vote` takes no amount parameter (line 78-82). Line 111 `coin::withdraw<AincoreCoin>(account, weight)` moves that whole amount into `VoteEscrow` (line 119). coin::balance is the liquid CoinStore (coin.move:79-84), so a holder who calls `vote` is left with exactly 1 AIN. The repo's own test confirms this: core/executor/src/lib.rs:5544-5547 asserts `coin_balance == vote_gas_reserve` and `locked == balance - gas - vote_gas_reserve`.

(2) The release path is gated on `p.executed == true` and that flag is unreachable for the only supported action type. `claim_vote_tokens` (governance.move:140-165) reads `escrow.proposal_id`, scans GovernanceState, and hard-asserts `is_executed` at line 160. The only writer of `executed = true` is `execute_proposal` (line 188) — grep over the whole repo shows no other writer and no other `move_from<VoteEscrow>` (only line 163). `execute_proposal` requires: 1M AIN quorum (line 178), `votes_for > votes_against` (line 181), and — for `action_type == 1`, the only defined action per the struct comment at line 23 — it calls `epoch::update_epoch_duration(account, ...)` (line 185), which asserts `signer::address_of(account) == @0x1` (epoch.move:44). The executor binds every leading &signer slot to the authenticated tx sender via bind_signer_args (core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:463-467, 505-512), so a forged @0x1 signer is discarded; sender is additionally pinned to derive_address(pubkey) (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2464-2471). Therefore no ordinary account can ever execute an action_type==1 proposal, and every voter on it loses their entire balance permanently. Separately, ANY proposal (any action_type) that fails quorum or loses the vote is permanently un-executable, so its voters — including the yes-voters — are stranded too. There is no expiry, no un-vote, no admin recovery path.

(3) Reachability is direct and is the documented path. GovernanceState is created at genesis (core/node/src/genesis.rs:1031, verified at :574-577). Mempool applies no module allowlist to EntryFunction payloads (core/mempool/src/lib.rs:290-301). The JSON-RPC `aincore_vote` handler was disabled and explicitly redirects users to "submit a signed transaction calling 0x1::governance::vote via aincore_sendTransaction" (core/node/src/api_local.rs:1177-1181). The Rust GovernanceManager (governance/governance/src/lib.rs, driven by Executor::drive_governance at core/executor/src/lib.rs:1259-1265) is an entirely separate storage-backed system and never touches the Move GovernanceState resource — so it is not a rescue path.

(4) Corroborating tell: the repo's own escrow test only passes because it hand-writes `state.proposals[0].executed = true` straight into RocksDB (core/executor/src/lib.rs:5554-5556) before claiming. The happy path was never exercised through `execute_proposal`.

Severity: HIGH is honest, not inflated. Permanent, unrecoverable loss of a voter's full liquid AIN via a public entry function on a live chain, no admin escape hatch short of a hardfork. It is not CRITICAL: no theft (coins sit in the escrow resource, total supply is unaffected — test at :5548-5553 confirms no supply drift), no inflation, no consensus break, and it requires the victim to voluntarily call `vote`. It is materially worse in the launch context the founder is walking into: reaching the 1M AIN quorum means irrevocably escrowing ~20% of the ~5M public float, and a single rejected or action_type==1 proposal strands all of it.
round2_verdicts.minimal_fix:
Two changes in core/vm_move/stdlib/sources/governance.move, both required:

1. Let the voter choose the weight instead of seizing the balance. Change `vote(account, proposal_id, agree)` to `vote(account, proposal_id, agree, weight: u128)`, drop the `available - VOTE_GAS_RESERVE` computation at lines 86-88, and assert `weight > 0 && weight <= coin::balance<AincoreCoin>(addr) - VOTE_GAS_RESERVE` before the withdraw at line 111.

2. Gate release on RESOLUTION, not execution. Add `deadline_secs: u64` to Proposal (set at create_proposal from `epoch::now_seconds() + VOTING_PERIOD`) and a `resolved: bool`. In claim_vote_tokens, replace the `assert!(is_executed, ...)` at line 160 with `assert!(p.executed || p.resolved || epoch::now_seconds() >= p.deadline_secs, ...)` so voters on rejected, quorum-failed, and never-executable proposals can always recover.

Separately (not strictly part of the sink, but it is what makes action_type==1 permanently un-executable): `execute_proposal` cannot satisfy epoch.move:44's `addr == @0x1` assert from a user signer. Either give 0x1::governance a stored SignerCapability for @0x1 and use it at governance.move:185, or make the epoch update a system-driven post-step invoked by the executor with auth_signer = system_address() the way deduct_gas/slash already are (core/executor/src/lib.rs:1437, 2009-2011).

Because escrow.proposal_id is overwritten on a re-vote (line 117), also consider keying escrow per-proposal (e.g. VoteEscrow holding a vector of (proposal_id, coin)) so an already-claimable escrow cannot be re-gated behind a later un-executable proposal.

round2_verdicts.title: chainid-env
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
The factual core of the claim holds; the severity does not.

WHAT THE SOURCE SHOWS

Genesis DOES pin the chain id on-chain: core/node/src/genesis.rs:928 `storage.put("sys:chain_id", &genesis_chain_id)?`, sourced from genesis.json (validated non-empty at genesis.rs:767-772). Local genesis.json:2 has `"chain_id": "AINCORE-MAINNET-1"`.

The pin is read in exactly 3 places (grep "sys:chain_id" across the workspace): consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:1133, core/node/src/genesis.rs:591 (genesis-identity hash input), and genesis.rs:1866 (a test). Nothing else.

Producer/verifier asymmetry is real and is the strongest evidence:
- QC/vertex PRODUCTION binds the storage pin first: dag.rs:1132-1155 `resolve_chain_id()` = `sys:chain_id` -> env -> genesis file -> "AINCORE-MAINNET-1"; used at dag.rs:1007 `chain_id: self.resolve_chain_id()`.
- QC VERIFICATION is env-only: consensus/consensus/src/qc.rs:213-215 `expected_chain_id()` = `env::var("AINCORE_CHAIN_ID").unwrap_or("AINCORE-MAINNET-1")`, with no storage handle. Every verifier calls it: sync/src/lib.rs:388 and :806, core/node/src/api.rs:253/:307, api_local.rs:946/:991, depin/bridge-rust/src/aincore_client.rs:139. The chain-id check is first and fail-closed inside verify_qc (qc.rs:235).
- TX validation is env-only in both gates: core/executor/src/lib.rs:17-19 `get_chain_id()` and its use at lib.rs:2440-2447 inside `execute_transaction` (consensus-critical: a mismatch returns None, so the tx is silently skipped and produces no state updates); core/mempool/src/lib.rs:182 duplicates the env read inline.

No enforcement of the pin over the env exists. I grepped core/node/src/main.rs, lib.rs, genesis.rs for any boot-time reconciliation: none. The only genesis-pin boot gate (genesis.rs:588-615) hashes `sys:chain_id` into an identity digest checked against AINCORE_EXPECTED_GENESIS_HASH, which is explicitly opt-in ("When the env var is unset the check is a no-op") and never compares against AINCORE_CHAIN_ID. No `set_var("AINCORE_CHAIN_ID", ...)` exists outside tests.

So (a) no guard prevents it, (b) it is not already fixed, (c) the pin exists and is deliberately preferred in one module and ignored in the other three — this is an inconsistency the codebase already resolved correctly once.

CONSEQUENCES THAT ACTUALLY MATERIALIZE
1. Single-node state divergence: chain-id validation runs inside block execution (lib.rs:2440). One validator with a wrong/unset env on a chain whose pinned id is non-default skips every tx other nodes apply -> divergent state root. This is live-relevant: the running testnet uses `CHAIN_ID="AINCORE-LATEST-FRESH-1"` (scripts/testnet-join.sh:28), not the default, so an operator who forgets the env on that chain hits this today.
2. Self-inflicted finality break: such a node MINTS QCs labelled with the pinned id (dag.rs:1007) but REJECTS every incoming QC as ChainIdMismatch (qc.rs:235), stalling the sync finality gate at sync/src/lib.rs:388.
3. Cross-chain replay: the signed message covers chain_id (lib.rs:2498-2506), so replay requires two chains to resolve to the SAME string. Because the default is the mainnet id, any secondary chain running with the env unset accepts mainnet-labelled txs, and a tx a user signs against such a misconfigured testnet is byte-identical-valid on mainnet (still gated by matching sender/sequence_number there).
4. Minor: the faucet/test-mint guard (api_local.rs:445-465) also trusts the env over the pin, so a mainnet node with AINCORE_CHAIN_ID mis-set to a testnet id plus AINCORE_ENABLE_FAUCET would unlock minting the pin would have refused. Two misconfigs required.

WHY NOT HIGH
No attacker-controlled input reaches this. There is no public entry point, RPC method, or consensus message that changes what `get_chain_id()`/`expected_chain_id()` return — the value is a boot-time process-environment read. Every consequence above requires operator misconfiguration first, and all failure modes are loud (explicit "Invalid Chain ID" prints, ChainIdMismatch errors, stalled sync) rather than silent. On the mainnet launch config specifically, genesis.json's pinned id equals the hard-coded default, so an unset env is benign there and the defect is latent. It is a real deployment-safety and determinism defect worth fixing before mainnet (the pin exists and is ignored; the fix is trivial), but it is a misconfiguration amplifier, not an exploitable vulnerability. MEDIUM.

Also worth flagging as a documentation defect: executor/src/lib.rs:15 says the chain id "defaults to TESTNET for safety" while line 18 defaults to AINCORE-MAINNET-1 — the comment states the opposite of the code, and docs/MAINNET_HARDENING_AUDIT.md:43 lists AINCORE_CHAIN_ID as a "known acceptable env read" for determinism, which this analysis contradicts.

round2_verdicts.title: genesis-identity-gap
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
FACTUALLY CONFIRMED, SEVERITY OVERSTATED.

What the hash actually commits to — core/node/src/genesis.rs:288-311, `genesis_identity_hash(stdlib_hash, version, chain_id, validator_set_json, epoch_block_interval)`. Exactly five domain-tagged, length-prefixed inputs. Recomputed on every boot from storage at genesis.rs:591-611 and compared to `AINCORE_EXPECTED_GENESIS_HASH` at genesis.rs:613-622.

OMITTED (claim is correct):
- `treasury_reserve` (genesis.rs:779-780, written to `0x1::treasury::Treasury` at genesis.rs:1110-1119). Not folded, and no other folded input derives from it.
- `sys:total_supply` (genesis.rs:1146-1147) and `ValidatorSet.total_supply` (genesis.rs:962-967). The #7 change the claim asks about — `total_supply = total_bootstrap_stake + treasury_reserve_amount` (genesis.rs:965) — is NOT covered: the bootstrap-stake half is only implicitly covered via validator_set_json, and the treasury half is not covered at all.
- `epoch_duration` (genesis.rs:781, seeded into `0x1::epoch::Epoch` at genesis.rs:993-1000).

PARTIAL REFUTATION of the "epoch params" half of the claim: the consensus-critical epoch parameter IS already committed. `epoch_block_interval` is folded at genesis.rs:305 and pinned to storage at genesis.rs:935-938 (SEC-#13), with a regression test at genesis.rs:1943-1950. Only the wall-clock `epoch_duration` is uncovered, and that one merely shifts `epoch_start_time` (epoch.move:32).

SECOND, UNCLAIMED OMISSION — a precision hole in the one input that *does* carry allocation: `validator_set_json` (`sys:validator_set:v1`) carries stake already integer-divided to whole AIN by `scale_stake_to_whole_ain` (genesis.rs:224-233, called at genesis.rs:245). So two genesis.json files whose validator stakes differ by any amount under 10^18 quanta produce a byte-identical validator_set_json and therefore an identical identity hash, while producing different `total_bootstrap_stake` → different `ValidatorSet.total_supply` and `sys:total_supply`.

IS THE DIVERGENCE ACTUALLY CONSEQUENTIAL? Yes. `ValidatorSet.total_supply` is the live emission anchor: staking.move:390-394 computes `minted = total_supply + cumulative_burned; remaining = MAX_SUPPLY - minted`, and the epoch budget is carved from `remaining` (staking.move:418-419, 471-472). Two nodes seeded with different treasury values therefore mint different rewards forever — a genuine hard fork, not a cosmetic difference.

AND NOTHING ELSE CATCHES IT AT BOOT. `sys:state_root` is a running hash chain seeded from a hardcoded all-zeros constant (executor/src/lib.rs:738-740, 1622-1631) folding only per-block write deltas — it is NOT a commitment over genesis state. Genesis never writes `sys:state_root`. So divergent-genesis nodes start with identical state roots and stay identical until a transaction touches the divergent keys.

WHY MEDIUM AND NOT HIGH:
(a) No attacker path. genesis.json is a local operator file (loaded from disk, genesis.rs:735-755). There is no public entry fn, JSON-RPC method, or consensus message that lets a remote party influence any of the omitted fields on someone else's node. A party who can rewrite your genesis.json already owns your node. A node booted with a divergent genesis forks *itself* off; the honest set is unaffected. This is not remotely triggerable, which is what HIGH would require.
(b) There is a late backstop. Once `distribute_rewards` writes the divergent `ValidatorSet`, state roots diverge and `sync/src/lib.rs:120` rejects on `block.header.state_root != summary.state_root`. So the failure is eventually loud, just at the wrong time and with a misleading symptom.
(c) The control itself is opt-in and off by default (genesis.rs:613; env unset = no-op, tested at genesis.rs:1881-1894), so this is a completeness gap in defense-in-depth, not a broken mandatory invariant.

WHY NOT LOWER THAN MEDIUM: the pin's own contract (genesis.rs:284-287) claims it refuses to boot on "wrong genesis.json", and docs/MULTI_VALIDATOR_BRINGUP.md:196 tells operators to set it on every node precisely so a mismatched genesis is caught. For the allocation fields it silently returns "same chain". Given the founder is about to stand up mainnet and seed a ~5M AIN float — treasury_reserve being exactly the number most likely to be hand-edited between node deployments — the one documented safeguard failing open on that field is a real operational risk worth fixing before genesis is frozen.

FIX TRAP (important): do NOT fold `sys:total_supply` into the hash. It is runtime-mutable — executor/src/lib.rs:1009-1010 stages it as a tx update, and lib.rs:1068 / lib.rs:1290 write it directly. Folding it would make the pin mismatch on every reopen after the first emission. Likewise `0x1::treasury::Treasury` mutates as tokens are sold. The folded value must be an immutable, genesis-only key.

round2_verdicts.title: sync-bytecap
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
The core assertion is correct: sync/src/lib.rs:1058 caps the sync batch by BLOCK COUNT only (`end_height = min(local_height, req.from_height + 500)`), and the loop at sync/src/lib.rs:1060-1067 accumulates 500 parsed Blocks with no running byte budget; handle_message then serializes the whole SyncResponse into one string (sync/src/lib.rs:1044-1046). No byte cap exists anywhere in sync/src/lib.rs.

REACHABLE UNAUTHENTICATED — confirmed, not theoretical. common/network/src/lib.rs:366-378 delegates every decryptable non-HELLO frame to the node handler; the signed-HELLO identity verification (common/network/src/lib.rs:276-357) applies only to `HELLO:` messages, so an anonymous peer that completes the ephemeral DH (common/network/src/lib.rs:153-198) can send SYNC_REQ. core/node/src/main.rs:749-759 routes `SYNC_REQ:` straight to chain_sync::handle_message. Existing throttles bound but do not prevent it: 100 msg/s per connection (common/network/src/lib.rs:207), 60 conns per IP (common/network/src/lib.rs:10), 100 conns total (common/network/src/lib.rs:6). One IP can therefore hold 60 concurrent sessions each issuing 100 requests/s.

AMPLIFICATION IS ATTACKER-CONTROLLED. Mempool allows 100 KB per tx (core/mempool/src/lib.rs:169-171) and there is NO per-byte gas anywhere in core/executor/src/lib.rs; 50 txs per vertex (consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:419); a block absorbs the payloads of every vertex in the commit sequence (consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:878-886). So multi-MB blocks are cheap to create and persist forever. A ~150-byte SYNC_REQ then makes the server read 500 such blocks from RocksDB, hold them as Vec<Block>, serialize to a full JSON copy, encrypt to a ciphertext copy, and build a packet copy (common/network/src/lib.rs:397-409) — roughly 4x peak. At 5 MB blocks that is ~2.5 GB of response data and ~10 GB peak allocation from a single unauthenticated request; the attacker need not even read the reply (write_all stalls with the giant buffer resident). Server-side OOM/remote crash is real.

CLAIM PARTIALLY REFUTED ON DETAIL. (a) "unbounded" is inaccurate — it is bounded by 500 x block size, not unbounded. (b) CLIENT OOM IS REFUTED: read_encrypted_msg enforces a hard 10 MiB frame ceiling at common/network/src/lib.rs:655 BEFORE the `vec![0u8; msg_len]` allocation, so the receiving side can never allocate more than 10 MiB per frame. Note the asymmetry: the server's inbound cap is 1 MiB (common/network/src/lib.rs:239) while the client's is 10 MiB.

SECOND, NON-ADVERSARIAL FAILURE AT THE SAME LINE (arguably the bigger mainnet risk): because the batch is count-capped only, once average block size exceeds ~21 KB a 500-block response exceeds the client's 10 MiB frame cap, read_encrypted_msg returns Err, and sync/src/lib.rs:717-723 breaks the loop. New and lagging nodes then can NEVER sync — no attacker required, ordinary DEX transaction volume triggers it deterministically.

WHY NOT LOWER THAN HIGH: on today's heartbeat-only testnet (empty payloads) this is inert, which argues for MEDIUM. But both trigger conditions — DEX volume, or an attacker cheaply fattening history with 100 KB txs — are exactly what the founder is about to enable, the fat blocks are permanent so the kill condition never expires, and the outcome is unauthenticated remote node OOM plus permanent loss of the ability to bootstrap new nodes. HIGH is honest. It is not CRITICAL: no funds are at risk, no consensus safety violation, and the existing count/rate/connection caps keep it from being a one-packet kill on an empty chain.

round2_verdicts.title: p2p-conncount
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
The increment/decrement asymmetry is real and exactly as described.

INCREMENT (core/node/src/p2p.rs:344-347): the per-host counter `inbound_connections_by_host` is bumped only inside the `ConnectedPoint::Listener` arm of the `endpoint` match, which is reached only AFTER the per-peer guard at p2p.rs:318-327. That guard does `swarm.close_connection(connection_id); continue;` (p2p.rs:325-326) — `continue` restarts the outer `loop` (p2p.rs:250) and skips the whole `endpoint` match, so an inbound connection rejected for exceeding `MAX_LIBP2P_CONNECTIONS_PER_PEER` (=2, p2p.rs:29) is NEVER counted.

DECREMENT (p2p.rs:367-379): `SwarmEvent::ConnectionClosed` decrements for EVERY closed connection whose endpoint is `ConnectedPoint::Listener` and whose multiaddr yields a host — with no record of whether that connection was ever counted. libp2p 0.54 (Cargo.lock:4064-4065) emits `ConnectionClosed` with the original endpoint for connections torn down via `Swarm::close_connection`, so every connection killed at p2p.rs:325 produces an uncompensated `saturating_sub(1)` at p2p.rs:373, and the entry is even removed at 0 (p2p.rs:374-376).

Direction of the error is toward under-counting, i.e. the limiter opens up rather than locking out. Concrete exploit from one IP, using only free libp2p identities:
1. Attacker dials twice with identity A -> counted, host count = 2 (at the cap `MAX_INBOUND_LIBP2P_CONNECTIONS_PER_HOST` = 2, p2p.rs:30).
2. Attacker dials a 3rd time with identity A -> `num_established` = 3 > 2 -> rejected at p2p.rs:318 without increment -> its close decrements host count 2 -> 1.
3. Repeat -> host count 0 while 2 live inbound connections remain.
4. Dial with fresh identity B -> increments from the deflated 0 -> admitted.
Each cheap duplicate dial buys one extra permanently-admitted inbound connection, so the per-IP cap of 2 is fully bypassable and live inbound connections from a single host grow without bound (fd/memory exhaustion on the node's libp2p listener). Note the sibling rejection at p2p.rs:348-357 is NOT buggy: it increments first, then closes, so its decrement is balanced.

Reachability: real. The libp2p listener is bound on 0.0.0.0:port+100 (p2p.rs:232-235) and is unauthenticated to any peer completing a Noise handshake; the attacker needs no stake, no validator membership, no valid tx. Nothing else caps it — there is no `connection_limits::Behaviour` in the `P2PBehaviour` struct (p2p.rs:171-180) and no other `close_connection`/limit anywhere in core/node/src. `with_idle_connection_timeout(20s)` (p2p.rs:196-197) does not help against a peer that keeps protocol streams alive. The LiDAR limiter (p2p.rs:287-306) throttles messages/sec, not connections.

Severity honesty — downgrading HIGH -> MEDIUM. The impact class is availability only: no consensus safety, no state divergence, no mint/fund path. And the mitigation being defeated was weak to begin with — a per-source-IP cap of 2 with no global connection limit does not stop a connection flood from multiple source IPs, and the Noise-handshake path on a public port is already DoS-able without this bug. What the bug genuinely changes is cost: reaching thousands of concurrent inbound sockets goes from "needs thousands of source IPs" to "needs one". Given n=3 validators where quorum is all 3 (so killing one node's networking halts the chain), that cost reduction is material and should be fixed before mainnet — but it is a defense-in-depth bypass, not a HIGH-impact protocol break.

round2_verdicts.title: qc-vote-binding
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
The claim is materially correct at the cited location, with one correction to the claimed mechanism's precondition.

**The vote store is not bound to the vote payload.** `collected_vote_key` = `consensus:qc_vote_agg:{round}:{signer_address}` (qc_producer.rs:257-259) — round + address only. The stored VALUE is the bare signature hex, with no copy of, or digest of, the vote it signs (`store_collected_vote`, qc_producer.rs:265-286, put at :284). `collected_signers` (qc_producer.rs:290-305) therefore returns signatures whose signed message is unknowable.

**Aggregation includes every collected signature unconditionally.** The loop the claim points at (qc_producer.rs:396-408) walks all collected `(addr, sig_hex)` and pushes each into `indices`/`sigs` with no check that the signature was made over the `vote` currently being aggregated. `build_qc(vote, …)` (qc_producer.rs:415; qc.rs:314-365) blindly `aggregate_signatures` — it never verifies individual signatures. `verify_qc` then does `fast_aggregate_verify` over `qc.finality_vote().to_signing_bytes()`, i.e. ONE message (qc.rs:303-308). A single signature over different bytes makes the aggregate invalid → `QcOutcome::Skipped`, no QC stored (qc_producer.rs:423-426). There is no subset retry, no per-signature pre-verification, and nothing ever deletes `consensus:qc_vote_agg:*` (grep shows no delete path), so the poison is permanent for that round in RocksDB. `store_collected_vote` even refuses to overwrite (qc_producer.rs:274-276), so the attacker's own later honest vote cannot displace it.

**Reachability — deterministic, no race needed.** The only payload binding is at qc_producer.rs:353-357, and it is conditional on `expected_block_hash` being `Some`. The caller derives it from local storage: `handle_remote_qc_vote` reads `block_{vote.block_height}` (dag.rs:1544-1555) and passes `None` when that height is not yet committed. `anchor_round`, `block_height`, and `block_hash` are all attacker-chosen fields of the gossiped `QcVoteMessage`. So a Byzantine validator picks a far-future `block_height` (guaranteeing `expected_block_hash == None`) and any target `anchor_round R`, signs that junk vote with its own real BLS key over the current epoch's real `validator_set_hash`. It passes the set-hash check (:347), passes the signer-in-set check (:360), passes the BLS check (:374) — because it genuinely signed it — and is persisted at `consensus:qc_vote_agg:{R}:{attacker}` (:380). When honest nodes later commit round R and their real votes arrive, aggregation at :396 mixes the poison in and `verify_qc` fails forever. `QC_VOTE:` is accepted from any peer over both gossipsub and the TCP server (core/node/src/main.rs:678-684 and :725-731 → dag.rs:1594-1597). Any stake weight works; only a validator seat is required. There is no equivocation slashing for finality votes (none in qc_producer.rs; dag.rs equivocation logic is over vertices), so the attack is free and unpunished.

The in-file doc comment at qc_producer.rs:326-330 explicitly asserts the `None` case is safe because "a vote for a different block … cannot combine into a verifying QC". That reasoning covers SAFETY (no bogus QC is stored — true) but is exactly backwards for LIVENESS: the inability to combine is the attack.

**Severity, honestly bounded.** This is a permanent DoS of the finality-certificate layer, not a fork or a chain halt:
- Leader election deliberately reads `step1_beacon`, NOT the QC-folded `last_vdf_output` (ordering.rs:707, with the audit-H-1 comment). So a node that forms a QC and one that cannot do NOT diverge on leader selection. No fork. This is the main reason it is not CRITICAL.
- Block production continues; `produce_and_store_qc` is side-effect-only.
- What does die: `consensus:qc:latest` / `consensus:qc:{h}` never advance, so the QC-gated finality path in sync never advances `consensus:finalized_round` (sync/src/lib.rs:410-431, served at :354), and the RPC finality endpoint freezes (core/node/src/api.rs:234-244, api_local.rs:927-937). That is precisely the artifact a bridge, light client, or DEX settlement layer is supposed to verify. On the live 3-validator topology no node holds >2/3, so multi-party aggregation is THE only path to a QC — one of the three seats kills it outright.

Existing test coverage confirms the gap rather than closing it: `vote_for_wrong_block_hash_rejected` (qc_producer.rs:760-785) only exercises `expected_block_hash = Some(...)`. The `None` branch is untested.

HIGH is the honest severity: cheap, permanent, un-slashable, one-validator liveness kill of the finality/attestation layer the bridge+DEX depend on — but no safety break, no fund loss, no consensus halt.
round2_verdicts.minimal_fix:
Bind the collected-vote store to the exact signed message so only signatures over identical bytes can ever be aggregated. In `consensus/consensus/src/qc_producer.rs`:

1. Add a digest of the signed payload to the key:
```rust
fn vote_digest(vote: &FinalityVote) -> String {
    hex::encode(&crypto::hash(&vote.to_signing_bytes())[..16])
}
fn collected_vote_key(round: u64, digest: &str, signer_address: &str) -> String {
    format!("consensus:qc_vote_agg:{}:{}:{}", round, digest, signer_address)
}
```
2. Have `collected_signers(storage, round, digest)` scan the `consensus:qc_vote_agg:{round}:{digest}:` prefix, so the aggregation loop at :396 can only ever see signatures over the vote being aggregated.
3. Pass `&vote_digest(vote)` at both call sites — the self-store in `produce_and_store_qc` (:205) and the peer-vote store in `collect_vote_and_try_aggregate` (:380) — and use it for the `collected_signers` call at :391.
4. Keep the `MAX_VOTES_PER_ROUND` backstop counted per round (scan `consensus:qc_vote_agg:{round}:`), not per digest, so a Byzantine signer cannot inflate storage by emitting many distinct digests.

Effect: an off-block vote lands in its own (unreachable) digest bucket instead of poisoning the honest bucket; honest votes still aggregate to a verifying QC. Additionally tighten the `expected_block_hash == None` branch (:353-357) to reject votes whose `block_height` exceeds the local chain height + a small lookahead, and add a regression test mirroring `vote_for_wrong_block_hash_rejected` with `expected_block_hash = None` asserting a subsequent honest quorum still yields `QcOutcome::Complete`.

round2_verdicts.title: block-persist-atomic
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
The claim's technical assertion is accurate in source, but its severity is one notch high.

NON-ATOMICITY CONFIRMED. Per commit in DagConsensus::add_vertex the order is: (1) consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:859 engine.try_commit(), which fsync-persists commit state at consensus/consensus/src/ordering.rs:627-659 (consensus:committed_rounds, consensus:cseq:{round}, consensus:finalized_round, consensus:finality_digest) — StateDB::put sets WriteOptions.sync=true, common/storage/src/lib.rs:117-119; (2) dag.rs:901 executor.execute_block_parallel(), which commits state in N INDEPENDENT fsync'd write batches, one per scheduled batch (core/executor/src/lib.rs:1595-1638), then a long tail of SEPARATE fsync'd puts: fee payouts (executor/src/lib.rs:1694-1729), process_fee_sweep_queue (1732), promote_downtime_attestations_to_slash (1738), execute_pending_slashes (1743), maybe_advance_epoch (1747, the staking mint path); (3) dag.rs:910 in-memory latest_block_height += 1; (4) dag.rs:937-939 save_block_json. save_block_json (common/storage/src/lib.rs:342-376) is atomic ONLY over block_{h} + latest_height + latest_block_hash + tx_index. The H-07 comment at dag.rs:928-936 claims crash-safety but scopes strictly to those four metadata keys — execution is outside that batch. The gap between the last state write and the block write spans multiple fsyncs and a Move-VM epoch-advance, i.e. milliseconds, not a nanosecond race.

NO RESTART RECONCILIATION CONFIRMED. dag.rs:268-275 reads latest_height / latest_block_hash and nothing else. Repo-wide grep for exec_height|executed_height|last_executed|commit_intent returns zero hits — no executed-height marker, no commit-intent record, no sys:state_root-vs-height cross-check. OrderingEngine::new_with_storage (ordering.rs:110-264) restores committed rounds from disk, so a round persisted in step (1) is never re-committed after restart.

TWO TORN OUTCOMES.
(A) Crash between step 1 and step 2: round is marked committed, vertices are in committed_set (ordering.rs:590,614), so they are never re-executed locally; latest_height unchanged. This one SELF-HEALS — sync re-fetches block H and re-executes onto the un-advanced state, producing a matching root (sync/src/lib.rs:974-997).
(B) Crash inside or after step 2, before step 4: state applied, latest_height still H-1. This does NOT heal and actively breaks recovery: sys:state_root is a chained transcript hash, SHA256(prev_root || batch_hash) at executor/src/lib.rs:1622-1631, so re-executing an already-applied batch yields a different root; verify_execution_roots (sync/src/lib.rs:94-136, mismatch branch at :120) rejects and process_blocks breaks (sync/src/lib.rs:976-997). The node stays on a private fork, and later same-height conflicts hit the SYNC_REORG_REJECT break at sync/src/lib.rs:869-879 / 904-923. Net effect: silent permanent state divergence and wrong balances served over RPC — directly relevant with a DEX reading balances. A mid-execution crash (between the per-batch write_batches at executor/src/lib.rs:1633) is worse: partial block state applied, then double-applied on any replay attempt.

WHY THE EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE DOESN'T REFUTE IT. (a) Graceful shutdown drains: core/node/src/main.rs:1012-1025 acquires consensus.write() (the same lock the mining ticker takes at main.rs:643) and flushes before exit, so SIGTERM/SIGINT restarts cannot tear — only SIGKILL/OOM/power-loss/panic can. (b) With empty payloads, schedule_batches yields zero batches so the loop at executor/src/lib.rs:1582 performs NO state writes at all; nearly every heartbeat block has nothing to tear. The clean 10-day resync is fully explained by these two facts and is not evidence of atomicity. Note the risk is currently inert precisely because payloads are empty and goes live the moment DEX transactions flow.

SEVERITY CORRECTION. Not attacker-reachable: no public entry fn, JSON-RPC method, or consensus message lets an attacker choose the crash instant; there is no remote crash primitive in this path, and the routine restart path is drained. This is a durability/integrity defect requiring a hard crash, not an exploit — MEDIUM, not HIGH. Aggravating factors that keep it above LOW: the failure is silent, unrecoverable without operator re-bootstrap, money-relevant at DEX launch, and per prior session notes the fleet has no systemd supervision (manual/hard restarts are the norm).
round2_verdicts.minimal_fix: Add a fsync'd commit-intent record so a torn commit becomes detectable and loud instead of silent. In consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs, immediately BEFORE the execute call at :901, write sys:commit_intent = {height: latest_block_height+1, anchor_round, root_before: current sys:state_root}; then clear that key inside the SAME WriteBatch as the block write by adding a batch.delete(b"sys:commit_intent") to StateDB::save_block_json (common/storage/src/lib.rs:342-376, e.g. before the write_batch call at :375). On boot in DagConsensus::new (dag.rs:268-275), if sys:commit_intent exists: if sys:state_root still equals intent.root_before, nothing was applied — clear the key and continue (case A, safe); otherwise state advanced without a block — refuse to start with an explicit operator message ("torn commit at height N; re-bootstrap from snapshot"). That converts scenario (B)'s silent permanent fork into a fail-fast halt with ~15 lines and no change to the execution path. The full fix (fold executor state writes and the block metadata into one WriteBatch, or add a per-height state-undo log) is a larger refactor and should be tracked separately.

round2_verdicts.title: dex-pool-squat
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
Every mechanical element of the claim checks out in source; only the HIGH rating is inflated.

1) Permissionless creation — CONFIRMED. `core/vm_move/stdlib/sources/dex.move:63` `public entry fun create_pool<X, Y>(creator: &signer)`. The only signer use is `signer::address_of(creator)` at :64 to derive the pool address. There is NO `== @0x1` check, no governance gate, no friend restriction (contrast `initialize` at :56-57 which DOES assert `@0x1`). Nothing in Rust gates it either: `core/executor/src/lib.rs:2318` treats `dex` as a generic recognized module for conflict-token purposes only, and `core/node/src/api_local.rs:669` merely prices `("dex","create_pool") => 120_000` gas. Mempool accepts any EntryFunction payload.

2) Registry key uniqueness is GLOBAL, not per-address — CONFIRMED. `dex.move:72` `assert!(!pool_exists(&registry.pools, &pool_key), EDUPLICATE_POOL)`, and `pool_exists` (:284-295) matches on `info.pool_key` ALONE, ignoring `pool_addr`. `pool_key` is the canonical `X_name::Y_name` (:265-282), with `bytes_lt` at :272 forcing one lexical order per unordered pair. So exactly one pool per pair can ever be registered chain-wide. The per-address check at :69 is a separate, weaker guard.

3) No removal, no deactivation, no admin override — CONFIRMED. `active` appears only at the struct field (:39), hardcoded `true` at creation (:88), and read at :261/:303. There is no setter, no `vector::remove`/`swap_remove`, no admin function anywhere in the 359-line module. Governance has no dex hook (grep of governance.move for dex: zero hits).

4) Not repairable on-chain — CONFIRMED and this is the part that makes it stick. `core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:420-422` and :478-482 both hard-refuse `publish_module_bundle` when `sender == system_address()` ("publishing to 0x1 is reserved for genesis/system upgrades"). So a squatted entry cannot be cleared by a Move upgrade tx; it requires a binary release plus state migration or a genesis restart.

5) Reachable right now — CONFIRMED. `core/node/src/genesis.rs:1136-1141` writes `PoolRegistry { pools: vec![] }` — genesis seeds NO pool, so the AIN pair key is unclaimed on the live chain. `genesis.rs:31` includes "dex" in `REQUIRED_STDLIB_MODULE_NAMES`, so the module is published and callable. The repo's own test at `core/executor/src/lib.rs:4745-4800` is a working PoC: an ordinary funded key (`SigningKey::from_bytes(&[35u8;32])`, not @0x1) calls `create_pool<AincoreCoin, WBTC>`, registry length goes to 1, and both the reverse-ordered and duplicate creates abort permanently ("reverse create abort is accepted and gas-charged"). Cost to squat: one tx and gas.

WHY IT IS NOT HIGH. The claim's phrase "blocks the real one" overstates the impact. What is blocked is a FOUNDER-OWNED canonical pool, not the DEX. `assert_registered_pool` (:256-263) matches `(pool_key, pool_addr)` against the registry entry, so the squatter's entry is fully usable: anyone — including the founder — can `add_liquidity`/`swap` against it. And the squatter gains no privilege over the resource: `LiquidityPool` has `key` only (no `store`/`drop`), Move resource access is scoped to the declaring module `0x1::dex`, and dex.move contains zero owner-gated functions and a hardcoded `fee_bp: FIXED_FEE_BP` (:78, :86). Holding the resource at your address confers nothing. So: no fund theft, no drain, no availability loss, no consensus impact. Real damage is (a) the official AIN pool permanently carries an attacker's address as `pool_addr`/`creator` in every RPC/indexer/SDK response (`api_local.rs:211-233`, `:1440-1457`), a launch-day trust problem; (b) the squatter takes the first-LP slot and sets the opening price, which the founder must arbitrage back on a dust pool before seeding 5M AIN; (c) it is permanent absent a hard fork. That is a MEDIUM launch-operations defect, not a HIGH security finding.

ADJACENT (same missing gate, worth a separate ticket, not scored here): because `create_pool` is permissionless, `registry.pools` is an unbounded append-only vector with no deposit, and `pool_exists`/`pool_status` are O(n) linear scans executed on EVERY dex call (:256-263). An attacker publishing structs at their own address can mint unlimited distinct type pairs and spam entries, inflating the single `@0x1 PoolRegistry` resource that every dex tx must deserialize. That one IS an availability risk and deserves its own verification.

round2_verdicts.title: dex-registry-unbounded
round2_verdicts.reasoning:
The data structure and the hot-path scan are exactly as claimed, and both halves are reachable from permissionless entry points.

STRUCTURE — `PoolRegistry` is a single global resource holding one flat vector with no cap and no removal path: core/vm_move/stdlib/sources/dex.move:27-29 (`struct PoolRegistry has key { pools: vector<PoolInfo> }`), entries at :32-40. `active` is written `true` once at :88, read at :303, and never set false anywhere in the module — there is no deactivate, prune, or admin function, so growth is monotonic and irreversible without a chain upgrade. Genesis seeds it directly (core/node/src/genesis.rs:1138-1141) and publishes `dex` as a stdlib module (genesis.rs:31), so this is the live path, not dead code.

HOT-PATH SCAN — every state-changing DEX op calls `assert_registered_pool` (dex.move:256-263), which does `borrow_global<PoolRegistry>(@0x1)` (:260) then `pool_status` — a linear `while` over the whole vector comparing `vector<u8>` keys (:297-308). Call sites: add_liquidity :101, remove_liquidity :162, swap_x_to_y :203, swap_y_to_x :230, get_reserves :251. `create_pool` scans twice-over (`pool_exists` :72/:284-295) and additionally rewrites the entire resource via `borrow_global_mut` + `push_back` (:71, :81).

GAS DOES SCALE WITH SIZE (this is the load-bearing check the claim depends on) — core/vm_move/src/gas.rs:84-94 `charge_load_resource` charges `load_base + bytes * storage_per_byte` = 10 + 2·bytes, with `storage_per_byte: 2` (gas.rs:19-27). The VM meter aborts with EXECUTION_LIMIT_REACHED once `gas_limit` is exceeded (gas.rs:48-60). Resources are read whole from RocksDB as hex and decoded per get_resource (core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:51-62). So per-op cost really is ≈2 gas/registry-byte plus ~10-15 gas per scan iteration.

REACHABILITY — `create_pool<X,Y>` is `public entry` with no permission check (dex.move:63-64); the only guards are per-creator `!exists<LiquidityPool<X,Y>>` (:69) and global pool_key uniqueness (:72), both of which are per-type-pair, not global caps. X/Y are unconstrained phantom params (`Coin<phantom CoinType>` has no ability bound, coin.move:22-24), and `coin::mint<X>(0)` succeeds because `dex` is a declared friend of `coin` (coin.move:14). Nothing checks that X/Y are real coins. So distinct pairs are free to manufacture: one published module with M dummy structs yields M(M-1)/2 registrable pairs (100 structs → 4,950 pools), and nested/vector type tags supplied as tx ty_args give unbounded distinct `type_name` strings with no publish at all. There is no allowlist of poolable types and no MAX_POOLS anywhere in Rust or Move.

QUANTIFICATION — addresses are 32 bytes/64 hex (api_local.rs:99-101), so a stdlib type name is ~86 bytes, pool_key ~174, and a BCS `PoolInfo` ≈ 420 bytes (attacker can inflate to ~1 KB with long identifiers). Registry load cost ≈ 2·420·N gas:
  • ~60 pools (≈25 KB) already exceeds the 50,000 gas_limit hardcoded in the CLI (core/cli/src/main.rs:482, :560, :628); transfers use 5,000 (:253).
  • 1,000 pools ≈ 420 KB → ~850k gas and ~850 KB read+hex-decode+BCS per DEX tx.
  • 10,000 pools ≈ 4.2 MB → ~8.5M gas per swap; cumulative registry rewrites to get there are Σ2·420·i ≈ 42 GB of state writes (create_pool rewrites the full blob each time), which is a WAL/IO amplification problem in its own right.
Attacker cost is negligible: gas is charged flat at `gas_limit × gas_price` (executor 2736 `let actual_gas = gas_cost;`) with MIN_GAS_PRICE 1 and 18-decimal AIN (genesis.json validator stake 1e24 against a 150M supply), so 8.5M gas ≈ 8.5e-12 AIN. The only admission gate is balance ≥ gas_limit×gas_price (core/mempool/src/lib.rs:212-232) — there is no protocol maximum gas_limit anywhere.

WHERE THE CLAIM OVERSTATES — "all DEX operations hit out-of-gas" is not permanently true for a client that can raise gas_limit: gas is effectively free at 18 decimals and no ceiling is enforced, so a bespoke DEX front-end can keep bidding more gas. The hard breakage lands on fixed-gas clients (the shipped CLI breaks at ~60 pools) and on node resources, not on an unavoidable protocol gas wall. Also note the DEX can never execute in parallel regardless: executor/src/lib.rs:2318-2320 pushes `dex_registry_key()` as a conflict token for every dex tx, serializing all DEX traffic.

Severity stays HIGH rather than being cut: no funds are stolen and consensus does not fork, but the growth is permissionless, essentially free, irreversible (no prune/deactivate), and it inflates both per-tx gas and per-tx node CPU/IO without bound on the exact feature about to be activated with the ~5M AIN public float. It is not CRITICAL — no mint, no fork, no halt.
round2_verdicts.minimal_fix:
Take the linear registry out of the transaction path and bound its growth:

1. O(1) membership. Add `struct PoolMarker<phantom X, phantom Y> has key { active: bool }` and `move_to` it at `pool_addr` inside `create_pool` (dex.move:74). Rewrite `assert_registered_pool` (dex.move:256-263) to
   `assert!(exists<PoolMarker<X,Y>>(pool_addr), ...); assert!(borrow_global<PoolMarker<X,Y>>(pool_addr).active, ...);`
   and drop the `borrow_global<PoolRegistry>` + `pool_status` scan entirely. Remove `PoolRegistry` from the `acquires` lists of add_liquidity/remove_liquidity/swap_x_to_y/swap_y_to_x/get_reserves so no DEX op touches the vector. Duplicate-pool detection in `create_pool` likewise becomes `assert!(!exists<PoolMarker<X,Y>>(pool_addr))` instead of `pool_exists` (:72).

2. Stop rewriting the vector on-chain. Either delete `PoolRegistry` and have the indexer build the pool list from `create_pool` receipts (the executor already decodes dex calls at executor/src/lib.rs:425-470), or keep it but bound it with `assert!(vector::length(&registry.pools) < MAX_POOLS)` — a hard cap is required, otherwise create_pool alone remains an O(N)-write amplifier.

3. Gate creation. Require a non-refundable creation deposit (or a governance/token_factory-registered token type for X and Y) in `create_pool` so pool slots cannot be minted for ~0 cost from arbitrary unconstrained type tags.

4. Drop `dex_registry_key()` from the dex conflict-token set in executor/src/lib.rs:2320 once step 1 lands, so DEX txs on different pools can execute in parallel.

final_verdict.mainnet_verdict: NO-GO. Two confirmed CRITICALs let any funded account mint AIN or permanently brick the flagship DEX pool for the price of gas, and a third makes the chain halt permanently the first time a second validator runs — which mainnet requires. The 349k-round "healthy testnet" proves almost nothing: genesis.json has exactly ONE validator, so no cross-node determinism, no QC aggregation, and no multi-producer consensus path has ever executed.
final_verdict.dex_verdict: NO — do not activate the DEX with the 5M AIN float. Today, any observer can permanently brick the AIN/WBTC pool with one gas-only transaction the moment it is created and before it is seeded (dex.move:115 write lands even though the tx aborts; the pair can never be re-pooled because create_pool's duplicate check is address-independent). Separately, transaction atomicity is broken chain-wide, so credit-before-debit sequences are mintable and transfers to unregistered recipients silently destroy funds. Minimum before activation: BLOCKER-1 (abort atomicity), BLOCKER-2 (conflict tokens), BLOCKER-4 (deterministic ordering — payload-carrying blocks are exactly what the DEX produces, and today they diverge), plus the dex.move write-ordering fix. BLOCKER-3 and HIGH-1/2 must also be closed before any multi-validator mainnet, which the DEX presupposes.

blockers.title: Aborted Move transactions commit their partial state (transaction atomicity is broken chain-wide)
blockers.file_line: core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:541-556 (session.finish() runs on the abort path); core/executor/src/lib.rs:2739-2757 (absorb_vm_result! stages vm_changes BEFORE checking $status.success); commits at core/executor/src/lib.rs:1604-1633
blockers.impact: Every assert! placed after a mutation anywhere in the stdlib is a live bug. Verified consequences: (a) coin::transfer to an address with no CoinStore debits the sender and destroys the funds — the receipt says "aborted" and the log literally prints "state reverted", which is false; (b) staking::withdraw_unbonded erases the unbonding entry and pays out nothing; (c) gas_limit is attacker-chosen and EXECUTION_LIMIT_REACHED (core/vm_move/src/gas.rs:48-60) enters the same non-fatal branch, so an attacker can stop ANY entry function at ANY instruction boundary and keep everything written up to that point — delegation::claim_rewards deposits rewards at delegation.move:299-333 before updating reward_debt, giving repeatable reward minting; (d) dex.move:115 sets lp_supply = 1000 on a zero-reserve pool from a reverted call, permanently bricking the pair (all later add_liquidity/swap paths die on the reserve assert at dex.move:119/208/235, no LP token exists to remove, and create_pool refuses the pair forever at dex.move:71-72 on a type-name-derived, address-independent key); (e) epoch::advance_epoch advances the chain clock even though it aborts. Cost of every one of these: one transaction's gas. No privilege, no capital.
blockers.fix: Split the single session in execute_transaction_actions (core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:462-557) into two, Aptos-style. Session G runs the must_succeed pre-actions (the coin::deduct_gas staged at core/executor/src/lib.rs:2667-2693), finishes, and its changes always commit. Session U runs the user payload; on Err, DROP it without calling finish() and return an empty user changeset with ExecutionStatus::aborted. Session G's resolver must overlay Session U's changes so gas applies on top of a successful payload and on top of untouched state after an abort. Share one AINCOREGasMeter so metering is unchanged; gas, sequence-number bump and the "aborted" receipt keep working exactly as today. Delete the false "state reverted" log at vm_move/src/lib.rs:545. Regression tests: coin::transfer to an unregistered recipient leaves sender at pre_balance - gas; a seeded Epoch resource is unchanged after a user-signed advance_epoch; add_liquidity(10_000, 10_000, min_lp=u128::MAX) on a fresh pool leaves lp_supply == 0 and the pool tradable. Note the four existing dex abort tests (core/executor/src/lib.rs:4834, 4902, 4978, 5056) all abort BEFORE any global write and therefore pass while the bug is live — they are not coverage.

blockers.title: Parallel-execution conflict tokens omit staking::ValidatorSet / SupplyStats — unbounded AIN mint
blockers.file_line: core/executor/src/lib.rs:2276-2300 (governance branch pushes only GovernanceState + VoteEscrow) and :2307-2322 (token_factory branch pushes only TokenRegistry + TokenWallet)
blockers.impact: analyze_tx's dependency set is what keeps rayon from running conflicting txs in the same batch. Because governance and token_factory transactions never declare 0x1::staking::ValidatorSet or SupplyStats, they are scheduled in parallel with staking transactions that do touch those resources, and the last writer wins on the whole resource. That is a repeatable withdraw_unbonded mint — unbounded inflation of the 150M-capped supply, i.e. total loss of the token's value proposition, reachable from ordinary user transactions.
blockers.fix: Add the staking::ValidatorSet and staking::SupplyStats keys (and any other resource those modules transitively mutate) to the governance and token_factory branches of analyze_tx. Safer near-term posture for launch: treat any 0x1 module that is not explicitly modelled as conflicting with everything — default-deny the parallel scheduler (unrecognized module => whole-state conflict token) instead of default-allow. Add a test that a governance tx and a staking tx in one block cannot be co-scheduled.

blockers.title: One-round fast-forward permanently wedges the whole network — and it fires with zero Byzantine intent
blockers.file_line: consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:816-821 (current_round = vertex.round + 1, persisted as latest_proposed_round) against consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:332 (parents are taken ONLY from current_round - 1) and :360-379 (stake-weighted parent quorum)
blockers.impact: CORRECTION to the earlier framing: the jump IS bounded (ABSOLUTE_ROUND_CEILING at dag.rs:631 and MAX_ROUND_JUMP = 10_000 at dag.rs:632, both checked at :637 and :649 before the fast-forward), so "unbounded round jump" is not accurate. The real defect is worse. A vertex just ONE round ahead makes every receiving node set current_round = R+2. Parents are drawn strictly from round R+1, which now contains a single vertex; stake quorum fails; try_create_vertex returns without creating anything and without incrementing (the increment is inside the success branch at dag.rs:562). No node will ever author a vertex at round R+1 again, so the quorum can never be met. The chain stops forever, the wedged round is persisted so restarts do not heal it, and it needs no attacker — one validator whose ticker or clock runs a round ahead does it. This has never been observed because genesis.json ships exactly one validator, so the fast-forward branch (vertex.author != self.node_id) has never executed in production.
blockers.fix: Do not let a single remote vertex move the local round. Either (a) fast-forward only to a round for which the node already holds a stake-quorum of parents (i.e. advance to max(r) such that round r-1 has quorum), or (b) advance at most +1 per tick and let the normal ticker catch up, keeping the stream-based catch-up the MAX_ROUND_JUMP comment already assumes. Additionally, allow parent selection to fall back to the highest round below current_round that HAS quorum, so a node can never be permanently stranded. Chaos test required: n=4 nodes, force one to emit a vertex k rounds ahead (k = 1, 2, 10_000), assert the cluster keeps committing.

blockers.title: Commit ordering is not deterministic across nodes — forks the moment blocks carry payloads
blockers.file_line: consensus/consensus/src/ordering.rs:503-510 (anchor chosen by round-robin fallback over whichever leader vertex happens to be in the LOCAL dag), :487-491 (committed-round partition depends on local arrival order), :755-772 (causal-completeness: the parent walk silently skips any hash missing from the local dag instead of deferring the commit)
blockers.impact: Three expressions of one root cause: commit output is a function of local network timing rather than of committed consensus data. Nodes select different anchors, partition committed rounds differently, and commit vertices whose ancestors they do not have — so they execute different transaction sets in different orders. With empty payloads (today) this is invisible; the state_root only diverges once blocks contain transactions, which is precisely the moment the DEX goes live. Consequence at mainnet: honest-only fork, divergent balances, divergent DEX reserves, and a beacon/leader-election split.
blockers.fix: (1) Anchor selection must be a pure function of (anchor_round, validator set, deterministic beacon) — if the elected leader's vertex is absent locally, DEFER the commit and fetch it; never fall through to a different leader because of local availability. (2) Gate the commit on causal completeness: at ordering.rs:763, if any parent hash is not resolvable in the dag, abort the whole commit attempt and request the missing vertices rather than pushing a partial history. (3) Make the committed-round partition depend only on anchor_round/finalized_round, not on insertion order. Acceptance gate: an n=4 cluster under continuous transaction load must report byte-identical sys:state_root at every height for 24h.

high_priority.title: Block header timestamp is recomputed locally on every node — breaks QC finality and sequential sync at n>=2
high_priority.file_line: consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:56-59 (SystemTime::now() inside new_with_roots, no timestamp parameter) folded into the header hash at :104; sole call site consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:911, which also passes the locally-scoped vertex.round (:913) and a local height counter (:910)
high_priority.fix: Make the header a pure function of committed consensus data: add a timestamp parameter (e.g. new_with_roots_at) and pass a deterministic value derived from the committed anchor (median of committed vertex timestamps, or the anchor vertex timestamp — vertices ARE author-signed, hash-bound and drift-checked at dag.rs:659-677, so they are a sound clock source). Also pass commit.anchor_round instead of vertex.round, and derive height from the committed sequence rather than the local counter. Without this, FinalityVote BLS aggregation (consensus/consensus/src/qc.rs:40-54, qc_producer.rs:353-357) only succeeds when all validators happen to commit inside the same UNIX second, and a restarting validator cannot sequentially sync (prev_hash mismatch at sync/src/lib.rs:264). Note this is a latent-until-n>=2 bug for the same reason as BLOCKER-3.

high_priority.title: Sync executes and COMMITS an unauthenticated peer block before verifying it
high_priority.file_line: sync/src/lib.rs:974-976 (execute_block_parallel runs first) then :977 verify_execution_roots; the state writes are already flushed at core/executor/src/lib.rs:1604-1633 including sys:state_root at :1631
high_priority.fix: The in-code comment at sync/src/lib.rs:978-991 correctly identifies that blocks are unauthenticated but only stops the node from HALTING — it does not stop the writes. Rejecting the block after execution does not roll back the RocksDB batch or the state root, so any peer can permanently corrupt a syncing node's state with one forged block. Fix: execute against a scratch/overlay state and only flush the WriteBatch after verify_execution_roots passes; or authenticate the block first (QC covering the block, or a proposer vertex signature) so a forged block never executes. Do not ship mainnet with nodes that can be bricked by a single peer message during sync.

high_priority.title: epoch::advance_epoch has no caller authorization and mutates before the abort
high_priority.file_line: core/vm_move/stdlib/sources/epoch.move:26-33 (no assert on signer, compare :41-48 which does assert addr == @0x1)
high_priority.fix: Add assert!(signer::address_of(account) == @0x1, 100); as the first line, before borrow_global_mut. With BLOCKER-1 unfixed this is exploitable today: the staking::cleanup_old_unbonding permission abort (staking.move:255-257) does not undo the clock advance, so any funded account can ratchet epoch::now_seconds() forward at epoch_duration per transaction (genesis epoch_duration = 10s) and thereby bypass the 21-day unbonding/slashing window (delegation.move:249, :263), the 7-day commission-change delay (delegation.move:344, :356) and governance timelocks (core/executor/src/lib.rs:1237-1252 -> drive_governance). Refuting the inflation half of that claim: distribute_rewards genuinely aborts (bind_signer_args at core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:565-612 makes a forged @0x1 signer impossible), so there is no mint here — the damage is timelock bypass.

high_priority.title: dex.move writes global state before its last assert
high_priority.file_line: core/vm_move/stdlib/sources/dex.move:115 (pool.lp_supply += MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY) sits above the asserts at :135-137 and both coin::withdraw calls at :139-140
high_priority.fix: Defense in depth for the launch-critical pool, independent of the VM fix. Compute-then-write: drop line 115 and fold it into the single mutation at :143, e.g. let minted_floor = if (first) MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY else 0; ... pool.lp_supply = pool.lp_supply + liquidity + minted_floor;. Then sweep the whole stdlib for the same shape (staking, delegation, governance, treasury, token_factory all inherit the atomicity break) and adopt a review rule: no global write may precede the last abort point in a function.

high_priority.title: Launch topology: genesis ships a single validator and there is no node auto-start
high_priority.file_line: genesis.json (validators array has exactly 1 entry, address e415306e..., stake 1e24) plus the known absence of systemd units on the 3-machine cluster
high_priority.fix: This is why the audit findings are invisible in production and why the testnet evidence cannot be used to clear them: BLOCKER-3, HIGH-1 and most of BLOCKER-4 only execute when a second validator commits. Mainnet needs n>=4 in genesis (BFT f=1), systemd units with restart-on-failure on every node, and then a payload-carrying multi-validator burn-in. Do not treat 349k empty rounds at n=1 as evidence of anything.

deferred: REFUTED — dex u128 overflow "cannot hold the 5M float": false. AIN is 18-dec (staking.move:38, api_local.rs:433) and WBTC 8-dec (indexer/src/main.rs:101), so assert_mul_safe (dex.move:322-326) permits ~680,564 BTC against a 5M AIN leg. The seed transaction and all realistic swaps pass with orders of magnitude of headroom. Real residual is LOW and functional, not security: the un-widened mulDiv caps subsequent add_liquidity/remove_liquidity at ~0.03% of reserves per call on a 5M AIN / 100 BTC pool, so exiting the founder position takes ~3,300 txs. Fail-closed EOVERFLOW aborts only — no mispricing, no theft, funds always retrievable. Fix post-launch with a u256 mul_div helper at the five sites (dex.move:120-123, :129-132, :174-177, :313-319).

18-dec/18-dec pools created via token_factory (decimals <= 18, token_factory.move:77) ARE unusable — the initial-seed guard caps the geometric mean of deposits at ~18.45 tokens. Not reachable for AIN/WBTC; fix with the same u256 mul_div before permissionless token listings are promoted.

create_pool (dex.move:63-90) is permissionless and unauthenticated, and the duplicate check keys on type names only (dex.move:265-282), so it is address-independent and squattable. Harmless once BLOCKER-1 is fixed, but consider gating pool creation to a governance/allowlist for the launch pair.
consensus/account/src/lib.rs AccountAbstraction trait still a stub; DA is sovereign-only; ZK/PQC not wired. All pre-existing roadmap gaps, none of them launch blockers.
Post-launch: add a chain-wide invariant monitor that recomputes total AIN supply from CoinStores each epoch and alerts on any drift from SupplyStats — cheap insurance against a missed mint path.
fix_order: 1. BLOCKER-1 — abort atomicity (two-session split in core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:462-557 + absorb_vm_result! in core/executor/src/lib.rs:2739-2757). Do this FIRST: it closes the DEX brick, the fund-destroying transfer, the gas-limit truncation mint and the epoch clock ratchet in one change. ~2-3 days for one senior Rust/Move engineer, most of it in the overlay resolver for the gas session. Ship with the three named regression tests.

2. BLOCKER-2 — conflict tokens in analyze_tx (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2276-2322). Independent of #1, can run in parallel with a second engineer. Prefer the default-deny scheduler posture for launch; it is smaller, safer, and costs only throughput on a chain that is currently doing zero TPS. ~1-2 days.

3. BLOCKER-3 — quorum-gated round fast-forward (consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:816 + parent fallback at :332). Must land before any second validator is started, or the chain wedges on the first ticker skew. ~1-2 days plus the chaos test.

4. HIGH-1 — deterministic block header (consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:56 + dag.rs:910-913). Small change, but it is the precondition for QC finality certificates to aggregate at all, so do it before the n=4 burn-in. ~1 day.

5. BLOCKER-4 — deterministic ordering: canonical anchor, defer-on-missing-leader, causal-completeness gate (consensus/consensus/src/ordering.rs:487, 503, 763). Largest and riskiest item; ~1 week, and it needs the n=4 loaded cluster from step 7 to validate. Do not compress this one.
6. HIGH-2 — sync: overlay execution, flush only after verify_execution_roots passes (sync/src/lib.rs:974 + core/executor/src/lib.rs:1633). ~2 days.
7. HIGH-3/4 — epoch.move:26 authorization assert and dex.move:115 write-after-assert, plus a full stdlib sweep for global-write-before-abort-point. ~2 days including the sweep.

8. Ops gate — regenerate genesis with n>=4 validators, systemd units with restart-on-failure on every machine, then a 7-day multi-validator burn-in under continuous synthetic transaction load with a per-height cross-node assertion on sys:state_root AND block header hash. No divergence, no wedge, no missed QC for the full window.

9. Only then: create the AIN/WBTC pool and seed the 5M float — with the seeding transaction submitted in the same block as create_pool, or with pool creation gated to governance, so nothing can land between creation and seeding.
10. Re-audit after the fixes. BLOCKER-1 changes the semantics of every transaction in the system; that deserves a fresh pass, not a diff review.
final_verdict.summary:
Twelve findings survive adversarial verification; four are launch-stopping. The chain has one systemic defect that generates most of them: aborted Move transactions commit their partial writes (core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:553 finishes the session on the abort path, core/executor/src/lib.rs:2741 stages the changeset before checking status). That is a break in transaction atomicity itself, so every assert! that sits after a mutation anywhere in the stdlib is a live bug — and because gas_limit is attacker-chosen and gas exhaustion enters the same branch, an attacker can stop any entry function at any instruction and keep what was written. It gives away a free, permanent, unrecoverable brick of the DEX pool (dex.move:115), silent destruction of funds on transfers to unregistered recipients, repeatable reward minting via delegation::claim_rewards, and a chain-clock ratchet that bypasses the 21-day unbonding and slashing window. Independently, the parallel scheduler's conflict tokens omit staking::ValidatorSet/SupplyStats for governance and token_factory transactions (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2276-2322), which is an unbounded AIN mint against a supposedly 150M-capped supply.

Consensus is not ready for more than one validator, and mainnet is by definition more than one validator. I re-checked the round fast-forward claim and must correct the earlier framing in the founder's favour on the detail and against him on the conclusion: the jump IS bounded (MAX_ROUND_JUMP = 10_000, dag.rs:632), but bounds are irrelevant — a vertex just ONE round ahead pushes every node to a round whose predecessor can never reach parent quorum (dag.rs:816 vs dag.rs:332), and try_create_vertex then stops advancing forever, with the wedged round persisted across restarts. That needs no attacker; a validator with a fast ticker does it. Add to that non-deterministic commit ordering (ordering.rs:487/503/763) and a block header that each node recomputes from its own wall clock (blockchain/src/lib.rs:56), and you get forks and failed QC aggregation the moment a second producer exists and blocks carry real payloads.

The reassuring operational evidence is void. genesis.json contains exactly one validator, so the multi-producer code paths where these bugs live have never run in 349k rounds of empty heartbeat mining. Treat the testnet as an uptime demo, not as a safety argument.

Estimate: roughly 3 focused weeks for two engineers to close the four blockers and five highs, plus a 7-day n>=4 burn-in under load with per-height cross-node state-root and block-hash equality assertions. I refuted one HIGH outright — the DEX u128 overflow does not prevent seeding the 5M float (AIN is 18-dec, WBTC 8-dec; the guard permits ~680k BTC against a 5M AIN leg); it is a LOW functional annoyance capping later liquidity moves at ~0.03% of reserves per call. Fix it after launch, not before.
